directions.name: Painted Fresh (Street Print)
directions.oneLine: psst. becomes a pocketful of Miami street print: a hand-painted ventanita board for right now, a wheat-paste wall of flyers for the week, a thermal receipt for your trip and a sticker for every place you went, all lit by the real Miami sun at the hour you pick.
critiqueOfCurrent: desktop-plan.png, desktop-wall.png, desktop-you.png, desktop-event.png, desktop-move.png: the map disappears on every tab except Now, so about 1,000 of 1,440px is empty navy. On desktop the product is a 440px phone panel floating in a void. desktop-move.png doesn't even show a move sheet; it's identical to Now at 10pm, so either the sheet failed to open or the capture is wrong.

mobile-wall.png and desktop-wall.png: flyer titles break mid-word ('THUNDE / RCAT', 'COUNTR / Y, NEW') because Flyer.svelte sets .title { overflow-wrap: anywhere }. Footers truncate ('MIAMI BEAC…', 'CLUB SPACE (…'). The best idea in the app ships with its most visible bug.

mobile-plan-scrolled.png, mobile-receipt.png, desktop-receipt.png: the planner books 'Sunrise swim off Virginia Key' at 6:15pm labeled DINNER and 'The 3:05 cafecito' at 5:06pm labeled SUNSET. Sun, Mon and Tue print as empty days, every one at 79° with no forecast/typical label. The promise is the right move at the right moment, and the receipt shows the opposite.

Every Now shot (desktop-now-day.png, desktop-now-night.png, mobile-now-night.png): two clocks disagree. The chip says 'MIA 4:42pm' while the giant numerals say 1:30pm or 11:15pm next to engineer jargon ('SCRUBBING · DAYLIGHT'). The largest type on screen is a slider value, not now.

desktop-now-day.png, mobile-now-day.png: day mode is mint water, gray roads and a white glass panel, which could be any SaaS map. Labels collide ('ALLAPATTAHDESIGN DISTRICT'), get clipped ('MID-BEA', 'NORTH' under the chip) and sit on coastline strokes. The only brand color, the sun yellow #FFC53D (oklch hue 84.1), is within 2° of Bumble's #FFC629 (86.2), so it isn't owned.

desktop-now-golden.png, mobile-move.png: the locked secret is blurred text ('Somewhere you should not know about'), which reads as a rendering bug, not a secret. Each list row stacks four metadata systems (caps hood, 'lowkey' pill, 'open · best 3:05pm', five orange pips plus $) in 10–12px mono, and none of them is the hero.

desktop-you.png plus every list row: the stickers are abstract gradient app icons (squiggle circle, wave blob, keyhole hexagon). Nothing about them feels collectible or Miami. 'You' is a light-gray form ('PINA-XXXXX' + Redeem) over a dark blurred void, the only light panel on a dark page.

mobile-now-day.png, mobile-plan.png, desktop-plan.png: the chrome is template. Six filter pills wrap, with 'Cheap' orphaned and cut off by the tab bar. The tab bar is a stock four-icon bar with a yellow pill. Native date/time inputs (11/20/2026 with calendar icons) and a range slider make 'Your stay, built like a DJ set' look like a booking form. Nine identical event pills, a 10px pineapple, and three fonts (Anybody, Figtree, DM Mono) that follow no object logic.
directions.concept: Concept sentence: "The friend who knows Miami doesn't send you a link. They hand you paper." Miami's useful information lives in print: the ventanita's board, the flyer on the pole, the receipt, the sticker from the place. psst. becomes that pocketful of paper, and the real sun shows on it, because the shade under every painted letter follows Miami's actual sun position at the hour on the dial. This extends 'the friend who knows Miami': a friend's tip is physical and specific (an hour, a price tier, a door), so every object carries a time and a place, never a vibe. Proof points, all checked this session: 'psst' is the whisper; the pineapple period becomes the price-gun label the friend slaps on the right thing; the 3:05 cafecito is a City of Miami-proclaimed break that started at Versailles' ventanita in 2014; Little Haiti's hand-painted sign tradition (Serge Toussaint, 2016 Florida Folk Heritage Award); William Lane's lifeguard-tower colors; Tilt Warp, the display face, was literally drawn as peeling pop-up-shop vinyl. What it is NOT: Miami Vice neon, grunge or coffee-stain texture, fake handwriting, Spanglish jokes. Keep from r0, re-skinned: the OSM canvas map and its traffic, the sun dial and Play the day, the receipt and PINA code, the flyer generator, the lean-in hold, and lines like 'Golden hour. Face west and stop talking.'

voice.register: Painted-sign deadpan: short declarative lines, each carrying an hour, a price tier or a door. The friend talking low. Bilingual only where Miami really is: Spanish nouns for real things (colada, ventanita, pastelito, HOY on the board), never Spanglish for flavor. One joke per object at most, and only in the footer position (receipt tail, flyer foot), never in buttons or errors.
voice.heroLine: HOY, 4:42PM. Two good moves before the sun goes at 7:06. One after, if you lean in. (Generated from data: time, ranked count, sunset, locked count.)
voice.errorLine: Lost signal. The board still shows what was good at 4:42PM. Times may have moved.
voice.receiptLine: 4 NIGHTS · 9 MOVES · 1 SECRET · NO REFUNDS ON SUNSETS

typography.why: Google's description: 'inspired by the dimensional lettering found in storefront signage… a sign painter's geometric sans serif… built up with a brush.' The Tilt article calls Warp 'stick-on vinyl lettering… a Pop-up Shop sign… inevitably peels over time', and the rotation axes make it peel. That is psst.'s subject (pop-ups, storefronts) and its interaction (peel, tear). The YROT axis drives the sun device. Scale (mobile/desktop): 88/120 board 'HOY', 44/56 view titles, 32/40 section titles; line-height 0.9; tracking -1%; YROT clamped ±14° for text, ±30° only in the intro.

It is quieter than the three print faces, so the objects stay loud while the instructions stay readable. 17px/1.45 mobile, 16px/1.5 desktop, 500 for buttons, 700 for inline emphasis.

color.ownedAccent: accent/pina, chrome-yellow sign enamel #FFB01F, oklch(0.813 0.165 75.1). It is the ventanita board and the pineapple period. Rule written into tokens: one piña object per view (the HOY board on Now, otherwise the active tab plus at most one price-gun label). Maximal color lives in the content (flyers, stickers, map), never in the chrome; the chrome is paper plus coal ink. At night piña hands off to uv/pina. P3 boost: in @media (color-gamut: p3), redeclare uv/* with chroma +0.04 and check on an iPhone. Those P3 values are not yet verified in gamut.
color.nearestCompetitorColor: Bumble yellow #FFC629, oklch(0.855 0.166 86.2) per brandcolorcode.com, from the adjacent social-discovery category. Piña is 11° warmer in hue (75.1 vs 86.2) and 0.04 darker, so it reads marigold enamel, not lemon-gold. IMDb #F5C518 sits at hue 90.4 (15° away). r0's #FFC53D (hue 84.1) is effectively Bumble's yellow, which is why it changes. Red is avoided entirely because the city-guide and booking category crowds it (Yelp, Resy, OpenTable, Time Out; from memory, not re-checked hex by hex this session).
color.dayNight: Driven by the existing daylight(t) plus a new solar altitude/azimuth function. DAY: sun-bleached print, with thermal and newsprint papers and full-strength enamel inks. The sun shade is short and falls straight down at noon. GOLDEN (altitude under 10°): papers color-mix toward light/golden in oklch, shades stretch sideways (to the right when the sun is in the west), and map water halftone warms 20% toward fire. SUNSET to NIGHT (altitude crosses -2°): BLACKLIGHT. Papers flip to coal, inks swap to uv/*, and the drop shade becomes a 0-offset uv/pink glow (blur 10px). That is the only glow in the system, and it's justified because it is literally blacklight on fluoro ink. Map roads go uv with the existing traffic lights in uv/pink (tail) and uv/pina (head) under 'lighter' compositing. AFTER-HOURS (3–5:30am): same coal papers, uv inks desaturated 30%. Real time crosses over about 40 minutes around sunset; scrubbing cross-fades in 300ms; reduced motion swaps instantly.

graphicDevices: THE SUN SHADE (primary, recognizable with the logo covered): every Tilt Warp headline wears a sign-painter's hard drop shade in a second ink (fire on day papers, coal on piña, uv/pink glow at night), built from stacked text-shadows: 1px steps, 0 blur, n = ceil(hypot(dx,dy)), max 15. The offset comes from the real sun for Miami (25.7617, -80.1918) at the dial hour, treating the sign as a south-facing storefront. h = sunAzimuth − 180° (+ = sun in the west); dx = 12·sin(h) px (shade falls right at sunset, left in the morning); dy = 3 + 9·sin(altitude) px (long drop at noon, short at dusk); altitude ≤ 0 gives the night glow. Tilt Warp YROT = clamp(0.15·h, −14°, 14°), so letters peel toward the light (Clymer's own concept for Warp; confirm the sign on device). Paper objects on the table cast the same vector at 1/3 length, 10px blur, coal 22%. WHERE: board header, view titles, wordmark, flyer numerals, at most 3 per view. NEVER: body text, list items, buttons, anything under 28px.

CUT LINES (secondary): every boundary is a print-finishing mark, never a 1px hairline or a rounded card. Perforation: 2px dots every 6px, with 10px half-circle notches cut into both edges (CSS radial-gradient mask), between ticket body and stub and between receipt days. Torn edge: SVG mask path, seeded jagged, 3–6px amplitude, on tear-off tabs, the receipt tail and peeled tape. Crop marks: 8px L-marks in coal at the four corners of the selected or focused object, instead of glows. Radius tokens are 0 and 2px only.

THE DOMINO (data glyph, from Domino Park / Máximo Gómez Park on Calle Ocho): energy and cost as one 28×14px tile. Left half is energy pips 1–5, right half is cost pips 1–4, coal on thermal (night: uv/lime on coal-2). It binds to m.energy and m.cost only; psst. never paints a dollar price it hasn't verified. The first tile in every list carries a 10px Martian Mono legend 'ENERGY | $'; aria-label 'energy 4 of 5, cost 2 of 4'. It replaces the five orange pips and the '$$$' string.

SUPPORTING TEXTURE (strictly limited): paper grain is one 256px feTurbulence tile rendered once to a canvas data URL and multiplied at 5% on papers. Flyers get a 1px riso misregistration on their second ink. Masking tape appears only on lean-in secrets. No stains, rust, crumples, fake handwriting or tape elsewhere.
signatureComponents: HOY BOARD (Now). A chrome-yellow (accent/pina) enamel menu board, full width on mobile (16px gutters) and 440px in desktop cols 1–4, square corners, paper grain. Header: 'HOY' in Tilt Warp 88px with the sun shade, plus a right-aligned live line 'FRI OCT 2 · 4:42PM' in Martian Mono 700, wdth 75, 15px. Under it, the generated hero line in Atkinson 17px (voice.heroLine template). SUN RAIL (replaces the Dial UI, keeps its logic): a 56px painted ruler with 24 hour ticks, sunrise/sunset ticks labeled in Martian Mono 11px, hourly rain as 2px bay strokes, and a 44px round sun-sticker knob (a moon sticker after sunset). While scrubbing, the header reads 'AT 9:30PM' and a 'BACK TO NOW' rubber stamp appears; the live clock is never replaced by a scrubbed time. 'PLAY THE DAY' is a stamp too. FILTERS: one non-wrapping row of five rubber-stamp toggles, CHILL · SOCIAL · WILD · $ · RAIN-OK, each 64×44px with a fire 2px outline and filled when pressed (aria-pressed). STRIPS, one per ranked move, like the slide-in rows of a cafeteria letter board: 72px min height, 2px grooves (coal at 12%) between rows. Line 1: name in League Gothic 30px uppercase, a dotted leader, and the best time right-aligned in Martian Mono 700 16px ('3:05PM'). Line 2: hood in Martian Mono 11px caps, then the domino, then status ('OPEN TIL 7PM' in leaf, or 'OPENS 11PM'). The top-ranked strip gets the friend's tip on a piña price-gun label overlapping its right edge ('GO AT 3:05', Martian Mono 700 12px, rotated -3°). LOCKED SECRET: the name is covered by a strip of masking tape (newsprint at 92%, torn ends) stamped 'PSST · HOLD TO PEEL · 3 LEFT'. Holding for 950ms peels it left to right (clip-path inset plus a moving curl shadow); Enter or Space does the same. The r0 lean variable (--lean, set in MoveCard.svelte and read by Logo.svelte as font-stretch on Anybody) is remapped, because Tilt Warp has no width axis: at full lean the wordmark goes to YROT -30° and XROT +8° (it leans toward you), and the intro 'stretch' keyframes in App.svelte are deleted. CHANGEABLE LETTERS: when ranking or time changes, each strip's characters flip out (rotateX 90°, 90ms) and the new ones drop in with a 12ms stagger. Strips link to the ticket stub. The 'On in the city' block becomes a strip of three mini flyers that open the Wall.

WHEAT-PASTE WALL (Wall). A kraft wall with grain. Flyers keep the r0 generator but gain two things. FIT-TEXT replaces overflow-wrap:anywhere: for each title, try League Gothic wdth 100 down to 75, then size 64px down to 22px, and pick the first combination where every word fits the column (canvas measureText). Break only at spaces; footers wrap to two lines instead of using ellipses. INK FOUNTAIN: a split-fountain blend of two inks keyed to start time (before 6pm: piña to fire; 6pm–midnight: tower-pink to bay; after midnight: tower-lavender to coal). It's a real letterpress technique and the only gradient allowed in the system. LAYOUT: mobile is 2 columns of 171px with a 12px gutter, rotation ±3° seeded by event id, 10px vertical overlap. Desktop is 4 columns in cols 1–9, plus a narrow folded map in cols 10–12 with a pin per flyer in view (hovering a flyer pulses its pin). TEAR-OFF TABS: every flyer has a 32px fringe of 6 vertical tabs printed 'ADD · NOV 20' in Martian Mono 9px. Dragging a tab down 40px, or tapping the fringe, tears it along a seeded jagged path; it arcs into the PLAN tab (420ms) and the PLAN tab's count stamp increments. Removing the event from the plan regrows the tab. If the event falls outside the stay dates (for example, an Oct 3 tab torn while the stay is Nov 20–24), the tab flies to POCKET instead and is stamped 'HELD'. A polite status line says 'Oct 3 is outside your stay (Nov 20–24). Held in Pocket.', with an 'EXTEND STAY' stamp that widens the dates to include it. With no stay set, every tab goes to Pocket. The fringe is one button: aria-label 'Add Thundercat, Fri Oct 2, to your plan'. Tapping the flyer face peels it off the wall (rotateX 0 to -18°, translateY -12px, 300ms) into the ticket stub. Date filter: a row of day stubs (THIS WKND · NOV 20–24 · OCT · NOV · DEC), not pills.

THE RECEIPT (Plan). The Plan tab is a thermal receipt printing. ORDER SLIP at the top: ARRIVE / LEAVE / LANDING / FLIGHT OUT as Martian Mono values on dotted rules; the native date and time inputs stay underneath, visually hidden but focusable and labeled. Energy is a five-stamp scale, CHILL to WILD, not a slider. BODY: 42 columns of Martian Mono wdth 75, 12.5px. Day headers read 'FRI NOV 20 ····· 79° FCST' or '79° TYP' (always label forecast vs 10-year typical). Lines read 'h:mmPM  NAME ····· [domino]'. The energy curve prints as a dot-matrix histogram, one column per hour, 3px bay dots. SLOT LOGIC FIX (required): a slot's hour and label come from the move's best time and opening windows; never place a move outside its window or more than 2h from its best time; empty days print 'FREE DAY · ASK THE BOARD'. TAIL: the last 40px carry the pink end-of-roll stripe (stock/tower-pink, 6px band, 8px in from the edge), a real thermal-roll warning. Then the PINA code as a perforated coupon with a real Code 128 barcode encoding the code. PRINTING: lines appear top-down at 18ms each (steps()), with an optional WebAudio thermal buzz (square wave 1.2kHz gated at 60Hz, 30ms per line, gain 0.04) and a tail curl (rotateX 8° on the last 60px). SHARE: draw the receipt to a 2x canvas and call navigator.share({files:[png]}) when supported; otherwise copy the text. Desktop: receipt in cols 1–4; the map in cols 5–12 draws the route as a fire marker line through numbered piña stickers, day stubs sit across the top of the map, and hovering a receipt line pulses its stop.

TICKET STUB + STICKER SLAP (Move and Event detail, feeding the Pocket). Detail is an admission ticket on paper/thermal: a body plus a 96px stub, separated by a perforation with 10px notches. BODY: a rubber stamp ('LOWKEY', 'LEAN-IN', 'CLUB') in League Gothic 18px inside a 2px fire box rotated -6°; name in League Gothic 56px; place and address in Atkinson 16px; 'THE MOVE' in Atkinson 19px/1.4; hours as a printed 24h ruler with open blocks hatched in leaf and a 'BEST 3:05PM' tick; sources in Martian Mono 11px. STUB, vertical text: 'ADMIT ONE · BEST 3:05PM · Nº 0A7F' (serial = hash of the id), plus the domino. ACTIONS: GET THERE (Apple/Google Maps links), SAVE, and I WENT. I WENT means dragging the stub right 60px or pressing the button: the stub tears along the perforation and the place's sticker slaps onto the map at its coordinates (scale 1.3 to 1, rotation -6° to 6°, ease-slap) and lands in the Pocket. STICKERS are redesigned as text-led die-cut vinyl: shape by category (round coffee, oval water, starburst food, ticket music, shield speakeasy), a 3px white kiss-cut border, one tower stock, and one word set on an arc in Tilt Warp ('COLADA', 'SWIM', 'LATE'). Event detail uses the event's flyer as the ticket's left panel. Desktop: the ticket overlays cols 1–5 at -2°, and the map zooms to the venue with a hand-drawn marker circle (SVG path, two loops, fire, stroke-dashoffset over 500ms).

layout.mobile: 390×844, phone first. HEADER, 52px plus safe area: wordmark 'psst' in Tilt Warp 28px with the pineapple drawn as a price-gun sticker period, ONE live clock 'MIA 4:42PM · 86° · SUN 7:06' in Martian Mono 12px, and a 44px SOUND stamp (off by default). FOLDED MAP strip, 152px, on HOY and POCKET only (on PLAN and WALL it collapses into a 44px 'MAP' stamp in the header that opens the same full-screen map, so those objects get the height): the canvas map cropped and shown as 3 accordion panels with crease shading, sun-colored, with stickers for moves open at the dial hour; tapping 'UNFOLD' opens it full screen. Map labels use greedy priority placement and are dropped if they collide, clip or cross the header. CONTENT: the active object at full width with 16px gutters, scrolling: HOY board, receipt, wall or pocket. Objects sit on the table color (newsprint by day, coal at night). TABS: four index-divider tabs, 64px plus safe area, each in its object's stock: HOY (piña), PLAN (thermal, with a count stamp), WALL (kraft), POCKET (tower-lavender). Labels are League Gothic 22px with a 10px Martian Mono sub-label ('now', 'stay', 'events', 'saved'); accessible names are in English. The active tab rises 6px and takes the sun shade. Every target is at least 48px. DETAIL: the ticket rises over the stack as a full sheet; drag it down or press Esc to put it back. No wrapping chip rows anywhere.
layout.desktop: 1440×900, 12-column grid, 32px margins, 24px gutters. The printed map is the tabletop under everything (full-bleed canvas) and is never hidden. HEADER, 64px: wordmark 44px at left; one live clock and the SOUND stamp at right. NOW: HOY board in cols 1–4, held by an SVG binder clip; map in cols 5–12 with a sticker for every move open at the dial hour; hovering a strip pulses its sticker. PLAN: receipt in cols 1–4, printing downward; route on the map in cols 5–12; day stubs across the top of the map. WALL: the wheat-paste wall slides over cols 1–9 (4 flyer columns); a folded map in cols 10–12 shows a pin per visible flyer. POCKET: a drawer of stubs, receipts and the sticker sheet in cols 1–4; map in cols 5–12 covered with the stickers you earned ('your Miami'). DETAIL: the ticket overlays cols 1–5 at -2°; the map zooms to the venue with the marker circle and a price-gun tip label. KEYBOARD: 1–4 switch tabs; ←/→ scrub 15 minutes and PgUp/PgDn one hour on the sun rail; Esc puts the ticket back; visible focus uses crop marks plus the coal/piña ring.

directions.motion: Motion is print: things feed, peel, flip, tear and slap. Nothing floats, blurs in or fades from nowhere. TOKENS: --dur-press 120ms (stamps, presses); --dur-ui 240ms (object moves, tab shuffle); --dur-paper 420ms (peel, tear, unfold), which is reserved for signature moments and is the one exception to the under-300ms rule for interface motion. Easings: --ease-ink cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) for moves and --ease-slap cubic-bezier(.3,1.6,.5,1) for stickers and stamps; --ease-feed is steps(1) per receipt line at 18ms. Letter-board flips: 90ms per character, 12ms stagger, at most 24 characters animated per strip. Sun-driven values (shade vector, YROT, paper warmth, theme) update per animation frame only while scrubbing or playing, otherwise every 60s; YROT changes are throttled to 30fps to limit re-rasterizing text. SOUND is synthesized in WebAudio with no files: stamp thunk, paper rip, printer buzz, letter clack. It is off by default, turned on by the SOUND stamp, and never autoplays. prefers-reduced-motion: no flips, peels, arcs, paint-on, curls or unfold animation, and states change instantly. The sun shade and theme still update, because they're information, but without transitions. Play the day steps hour by hour at 1s intervals instead of sweeping.

jawDropMoments.moment: Drag the sun and every painted letter's shadow swings with it: down at noon, long and to the right at golden hour, and the vinyl letters peel toward the light.
jawDropMoments.how: Add solarPosition(date, hour) to core.js (NOAA/SunCalc altitude and azimuth, about 40 lines, alongside the existing sunFor). In App.svelte, an $effect on app.hour sets :root vars --sx, --sy, --yrot and --warm. A shade(ink) helper builds the text-shadow list (n one-pixel steps along dx,dy). Headlines use font-variation-settings:'YROT' var(--yrot); papers use color-mix(in oklch, var(--paper) calc(100% - var(--warm)*100%), var(--light-golden)). It hooks into the existing Dial drag and Play the day. Reduced motion: same values, no CSS transitions, and Play steps hourly.

jawDropMoments.moment: At sunset the whole city flips to blacklight: papers go coal, inks turn fluorescent, the map's roads glow and the letter shades become UV halos.
jawDropMoments.how: Theme tokens are keyed by a data-light attribute (day | golden | uv | afterhours) computed from solar altitude. CSS swaps token sets and cross-fades with a 300ms transition on background-color/color only. MiamiMap.svelte gets a palette object per light state (land, water dots, roads, labels), and its existing 'lighter' traffic pass recolors to uv/pink tails and uv/pina heads. Inside @media (color-gamut: p3), the uv tokens are redeclared at higher chroma. Reduced motion: instant swap, no transition.

jawDropMoments.moment: Tear a tab off a flyer and it rips (with sound) and flies into your plan.
jawDropMoments.how: In Flyer.svelte, render a fringe of 6 tabs as one <button>. The rip is filtered white noise (AudioBuffer, 120ms) through a bandpass sweeping 3kHz to 800Hz, only if sound is on. The flyer re-renders with that tab missing (persisted state). Reduced motion: the tab disappears, the count stamp increments, and a polite live-region message announces 'Added Thundercat to Friday'.

jawDropMoments.moment: Your stay prints out of the top of the screen as a real thermal receipt, buzzing line by line, then becomes a PNG you can drop in the group chat with a barcode that actually scans.

A tail curl uses perspective plus rotateX(8deg) on the last 60px. Code 128 is encoded in about 60 lines of JS (start code B, checksum mod 103) and drawn as rects. antiTemplateChecks: 1 Font: PASS. Tilt Warp, League Gothic, Martian Mono and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next are all off the default list (no Inter, Geist, Roboto, Poppins, Montserrat, Space Grotesk or Space Mono). Each maps to one printed object: sign, poster/ticket, receipt, reading. Watch-out: League Gothic is a common free condensed. It's justified by its Alternate Gothic wood-type lineage and limited to names, flyers and tabs.

2 Accent: PASS with a guardrail. Piña #FFB01F (hue 75.1) sits 11° from Bumble's #FFC629 and 15° from IMDb's #F5C518, and isn't a library default. It FAILS if it drifts back toward r0's #FFC53D (hue 84.1), so the token carries that note.

3 Layout: PASS. There's no centered hero, card trio, logo row, pricing or FAQ. Every view is one of four physical objects (board, receipt, wall, pocket) on a printed-map tabletop, and the right side of desktop is never empty.
4 Device: PASS. With the wordmark covered, sun-directed drop shades on sign lettering, perforated cut lines, domino tiles and price-gun labels still say psst.

5 Decoration: PASS, conditionally. The only gradient is the split-fountain flyer ink (a real printing process, keyed to event time). The only glow is the night blacklight halo. The only shadows are sun-directed paper shadows. All backdrop blur is removed. This fails if anyone adds grunge, stains or tape beyond lean-in.

6 Voice: PASS. 'HOY, 4:42PM. Two good moves before the sun goes at 7:06.' sits naturally next to the error ('Lost signal. The board still shows what was good at 4:42PM.') and the receipt ('4 NIGHTS · 9 MOVES · 1 SECRET · NO REFUNDS ON SUNSETS'): time-stamped, short, deadpan.

7 Concept: PASS. (a) The shade direction is the real sun, because the friend who knows Miami knows where the sun is. (b) The plan is a receipt, because the friend hands you paper. (c) A tear-off tab adds an event, because that's how you take a number off a flyer on a pole.
risks: Kitsch or appropriation: Cuban, Haitian and Latin vernacular worn as a costume. Guardrails: no Spanglish or Kreyòl jokes, no fake handwriting, no imitation of a named living artist's style. Spanish only for real nouns. For the shoot phase, commission and pay real Miami sign painters (for example, approach Serge Toussaint or the Big Brother Art School) to letter the HOY header and the board alphabet, and credit them.

Sun legibility vs maximal color: every text pair above was computed this session to be at least 4.5:1, except fire on kraft (3.51) and fire on piña (2.76), which are banned for text. Chrome stays paper plus coal. Test outdoors at full brightness before calling it done.

Performance on mid-range Android: stacked text-shadows, YROT axis changes, the canvas map with traffic and grain together. Mitigation: at most 3 shaded headlines per view, grain as a pre-rendered tile, YROT throttled to 30fps, and the map pauses traffic when unfolded off-screen. Test on a Moto G-class phone.
Domino comprehension: first-use legend plus aria. If testing shows people miss it, fall back to 'ENERGY 4/5 · $$' text.

Tilt Warp is single-weight and wide, so it's for 1–4 words only. League Gothic carries every name. Fallbacks if Google Fonts fails: 'Arial Black' for Tilt, 'Impact, Arial Narrow' for League Gothic, ui-monospace for Martian, system-ui for Atkinson. Check the layout with fonts blocked.

Fontshare/ITF fonts are ruled out. ITF Free Font License v2.0 (17 Aug 2026), read in full: it allows @font-face self-hosting, but Section 02 bars 'subsetting, format conversion' without written consent, and Section 03 requires embedded fonts to be non-extractable. A base64 font inside a public single HTML file is extractable, so it isn't safe. Velvetyne is OFL, but some fonts are CUTE-licensed (PicNic), and none was a sign-painter face. Collletttivo is all OFL (Necto Mono is a backup mono). Departure Mono (OFL) was rejected as trend-heavy and pixel-sized. The Neue Black was rejected because it is drawn from Chicago Freedom Movement protest signage, which is the wrong thing to borrow for nightlife.
Time honesty: shades, warmth and blacklight must come from real solar math; a scrubbed time must never look like now; receipt weather must say FCST or TYP; prices are only the m.cost tier.

Scope: the receipt PNG with a scannable barcode (L) and the paint-on intro (M) are the first things to drop if time is short. The sun shade, blacklight, the slot-logic fix, the flyer fit-text fix and the always-visible desktop map are the non-negotiables.

Unverified this session (from general knowledge; check before anything public): the P3 chroma boosts for uv/*; the sign of the YROT-to-sun mapping (verify on device); the pink end-of-roll stripe as a standard thermal-roll warning; split-fountain inking as the source of gradient letterpress posters; and Domino Park being Máximo Gómez Park on Calle Ocho. All are believed correct but were not sourced here.

Guardrail: never use Florida beach warning flags as a weather icon. They signal surf and marine hazards, and borrowing them for rain would mislead people about swimming safety. (Considered and rejected while designing; r0 doesn't use them.)

Fonts in the sandbox: the r0 screenshots were captured locally, so the only evidence that Google Fonts load inside the published Claude artifact is the brief's CSP statement. Open the published artifact and confirm all four families render, including Tilt Warp's YROT, before judging the design. The fallback stacks above cover a failure.
Process note: to read the ITF license, I downloaded Fontshare's Tanker kit (141 KB zip) into this session's scratchpad (streetprint/tanker.zip). It is not in the project and should not be used.

directions.name: NIGHT FLIGHT
directions.oneLine: psst. shows Miami the way you see it from the window seat, lit by what is actually open at this hour, and the friend next to you points at one light and says: that one.
critiqueOfCurrent: mobile-now-day.png and mobile-now-night.png: the app fails its core job on first paint. At 390x844, the map, the 1:30pm clock, two buttons, the dial, the headline, the weather line and the filter pills fill the whole screen, and not one move is visible above the tab bar. Someone on the street sees a clock, not a move.

desktop-plan.png, desktop-wall.png, desktop-you.png, desktop-move.png, desktop-event.png, desktop-receipt.png: the map, which is meant to be the stage, is an empty navy void on 6 of 9 desktop shots. I could not reproduce this on the current build: on 2 Oct, Wall loaded fresh and Now, then Plan, then Wall in one session both render the map. So it is most likely an artifact of shots.mjs, which reuses one page and navigates by hash only. But it is what the founder judged, so fix the harness and reshoot before the next review.

desktop-now-night.png and mobile-now-night.png: the plane-window idea is already in MiamiMap.svelte (its own comment says 'like the city from a plane window', and it draws 420 headlight particles), yet it still reads as a dark-mode map template: violet land, a cyan coastline with shadowBlur 10, orange roads and pink radial blobs. The code shows why. Each car is a 2.4px dot built with a new radial gradient per car per frame, so there are no streaks and no bloom. Only about 43% of the 420 cars show at 11:15pm, spread across the whole metro. The camera is flat top-down, with no depth and no reflections on the water. On a phone, the sheet (52% of the screen) plus the 64px tab bar cover about 60% of the map. The shots were taken with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, so the traffic is frozen in them; this motion critique comes from reading the code.

desktop-now-day.png and desktop-now-golden.png: day mode is a mint wash (rgba(0,150,140,.16) under white land) with grey roads at 10-42% alpha. There is no sun, no shadow, no water color and no heat. Golden hour only tints the background grey-green, because the map cache is either day or night and the two are cross-faded. The best line in the app ('Golden hour. Face west and stop talking.') sits on the least golden frame.

desktop-plan.png, mobile-plan.png and mobile-now-night-scrolled.png: this is the full template kit. A glass sidebar (backdrop-filter blur 22px), rounded pills for every control (tabs, filters, presets, the MIA clock chip), native <input type=date/time>, and rows of icon, title and meta (desktop-now-day.png). In the scrolled night view, event cards slide under the pinned dial with no backing and collide with its 12am to 12am scale. Cover the logo and this could be any map starter kit.

mobile-now-day.png: the brand is barely there. The pineapple period is 0.3em wide next to a 32px wordmark (about 10px on a phone) and appears nowhere else. The yellow (#FFC53D, oklch 0.854 0.157 84) is a stock golden yellow with no rule for when it appears: the Play button, the tab highlight, the date tiles and the flyers all share it, so it marks nothing. On mobile, the MIA chip also overlaps the map labels, and 'ALLAPATTAH' runs into 'DESIGN DISTRICT'.

mobile-wall.png: the Wall's flyers are the strongest idea in the app, and they break names mid-word ('THUNDE / RCAT', 'COUNTR / Y,'). Flyer.svelte sets overflow-wrap: anywhere together with a random width axis up to 140. All four flyers above the fold also come from the same yellow/orange family.

mobile-plan-scrolled.png and desktop-receipt.png: the planner breaks the promise of 'the friend who knows'. It puts 'Sunrise swim off Virginia Key' in the 6:15pm DINNER slot and 'The 3:05 cafecito' in the SUNSET slot, because planStay scores moves by energy and distance and never checks what the move is. Nov 22-24 print as empty days, each at 79 degrees, and the receipt calls the cafecito spot 'A Little Havana ventanita'. A plan with three blank days reads as broken. The r0 shots used placeholder spots; 43 real moves are in moves.json now (e.g. Bar AZ.85, Mac's Club Deuce, Club Space Terrace sunrise), so re-run the planner and add a check that a move fits its slot before judging.
directions.concept: Concept sentence: "psst. is the friend in the window seat: as the city comes into view they lean across you, point at one light, and tell you why that one." This extends "the friend who knows Miami" from what they know to where they're standing: above the city, at this exact hour. The product's job, the right move at the right moment, becomes a lighting model. Everything actually open at the dial's hour glows (glow() already computes this from real opening hours). The sun's calculated position sets the light. One light, the Beacon, is the move, and the pineapple period of the wordmark is that light (a symbol of hospitality, shown lit). By day it's the same window under a high sun: turquoise shallows, boat wakes, pastel neighborhoods. Proof: the name is the sound of someone leaning over. Miami's first air terminal (Pan Am, Dinner Key, from 1 Dec 1930) brought flying boats down onto Biscayne Bay, and the NPS describes its Art Deco frieze as 'winged globes and rising suns'. For 95 years the city has been arriving by air and by water, under a sun. The map is real OSM coastline and roads, and sunrise and sunset are calculated. Night Flight is a viewpoint and a lighting model, not a costume: no boarding passes, departure boards, seat maps, gates or 'now boarding' copy. That is the line the hotel metaphor crossed. Process note: the brand skill asks for approval after each step (concept, voice, type, color). This pass collapses them into one deliverable, so get the founder's yes on concept, then type, then color before anyone builds.

voice.register: The window-seat whisper. Short, present tense, timed to the minute and specific about place: a friend narrating what's below, deadpan with a wink. Numbers are exact, or labeled 'about'. One joke per screen at most, and every joke must carry a fact (a time, a place, a price). If a line is funny but not useful, cut it.
never: any airport pun (boarding, gate, final approach, cleared for takeoff)
voice.heroLine: Sun's gone at 7:06. Be on the water by 6:50.
voice.errorLine: Can't see you from up here. Pick a neighborhood and I'll point.
voice.receiptLine: Saved. It'll light up on your map when it's the right hour.

typography.role: Speaks: hero title cards, move names, the wordmark, tab labels, body text. One family for every word that talks.
typography.family: Science Gothic (variable: wdth 50-200, wght 100-900, CTRS contrast 0-85, slnt -10-0)
typography.license: SIL Open Font License 1.1, 'Copyright 2024 Font Detective LLC'. No Reserved Font Name is declared. It loads through the Google Fonts stylesheet the artifact CSP already allows, so it needs no base64; OFL would also allow embedding. Request: family=Science+Gothic:wdth,wght,CTRS@50..200,300..900,0..60&display=swap. The Latin subset measured 156,396 bytes.
typography.why: It revives Morris F. Benton's Bank Gothic (ATF, 1930-33), a face with film-title and signage history: Fonts In Use lists Bank Gothic in Tom Kan's Enter the Void title sequence. The revival adds a lowercase, true small caps and a 50-200 width axis. That axis puts the concept into one family: cinemascope-wide title cards at wdth 150-180, lowercase move names at 110-125, long event names squeezed to fit at 60-75, and body text at 95. I rendered it at real sizes in headless Chrome: a 64px caps hero, 12px credits at wdth 180 tracked 0.30em, and 16px body at wdth 100 / wght 420 all hold up. Stroke-only text at wdth 170 / wght 300 reads as a lit neon tube on night glass and as an unlit channel letter on paper, so no third 'neon' font is needed. Tokens: title-xl 40-72px fluid, caps, wdth fluid 110 to 170 by container width, wght 850, tracking -0.01em, line-height 0.9. move-name 24-34px, sentence case, axes set per move (see graphic devices). credits 11-12px caps, wdth 180, wght 500, tracking 0.30em. body 16/1.5, wdth 95, wght 420, max 34em. Long names condense automatically: step wdth down from 120 to 60 until the name fits on 2 lines, and never break inside a word (this fixes mobile-wall.png). Wordmark: 'psst' lowercase, wdth 125, wght 900; the existing --lean variable drives wdth from 125 to 200.

typography.role: Measures: times, temperatures, distances, opening hours, prices, credit lines, map legend
typography.license: SIL Open Font License 1.1, 'Copyright 2021 The Martian Mono Project Authors'. No Reserved Font Name. Google Fonts stylesheet; the Latin subset measured 38,392 bytes.
typography.why: Every fact in psst. is a reading on the clock: 6:42PM, 86 degrees, 12 MIN, OPEN TILL 2AM, $$. Monospace figures are tabular by construction, so times don't jitter while you drag the sun. The width axis lets long venue and address strings fit at wdth 75 instead of truncating. Tokens: label 11-12px caps, wght 450-500, tracking 0.02em; data 13px, wdth 87.5; clock 48-64px, wdth 75, wght 700. Never used for paragraphs. Rejected in testing: Doto (its dot-matrix digits read as an airport board) and Datatype (no advantage). Total font budget is about 195KB. Use display=swap with size-adjusted Arial fallbacks.

typography.role: Fallback display face, only if the founder reads the GTA association as too strong (see risks)
typography.family: Sprat (Collletttivo; serif with width and weight axes, 18 styles)
typography.license: SIL Open Font License, as stated on the Collletttivo page. It is not on Google Fonts, so it would be inlined as a base64 @font-face, which OFL allows. I did not verify whether it declares a Reserved Font Name: read the OFL.txt in the download. If it declares one, either embed the unmodified WOFF2 or rename the family internally when subsetting.
typography.why: A high-contrast serif after an Eric Gill lettering, running from condensed to wide and made for titles: a classic film title card with no video-game association. It is the second choice because it is elegant rather than playful and weaker as a body face; Science Gothic credits and Martian Mono would stay. Fontshare is excluded entirely: its ITF Free Font License v2.0 (17 Aug 2026) counts subsetting and format conversion as prohibited modification, allows document embedding only where the font 'cannot be extracted', and allows self-hosting only on your own server, which a single-file artifact doesn't have.

color.ownedAccent: Beacon #FFB127, oklch(0.815 0.163 75.0): the lit pineapple. Rule, written into the tokens as a usage note: beacon appears on at most one interactive element per view (the move you should make right now: its map pin and its Go button count as one), plus the wordmark period. It is a fill, and the text on it is ink-day. Everything else that glows on the map is 'light' (headlight, tail, pool, flamingo), never beacon. This replaces the current #FFC53D, which today marks the Play button, the tab highlight, the date tiles and the flyers at once.
color.nearestCompetitorColor: In the category, checked live on 2 Oct: The Infatuation's accent is #0066F1 blue (National 2 type). Places by Raya has no accent, only black, white and warm grey. DICE uses #F2EF1D lemon and #4BFA94 green. Bumble's live tile color is #FFF500 (oklch 0.947 0.203 106.7). None of them use amber. The nearest well-known amber, outside the category, is Amazon orange, commonly cited as #FF9900 (oklch 0.772 0.174 64.6). I could not verify it live because the site blocks automated fetches; beacon sits about 10 degrees yellower and 0.04 lighter. Locally, the Miami Dolphins are commonly cited as aqua #008E97 plus orange #FC4C02 (also not verified live), so never set beacon next to pool aqua in large adjacent fields.
color.dayNight: Driven by the sun's real elevation and azimuth, not by clock buckets. This is new code: core.js only has sunFor() for sunrise and sunset. Add a NOAA solar-position function (about 25 lines; lat 25.7617, lng -80.1918, America/New_York) that returns {elevation, azimuth} for any date and fractional hour. The map interpolates in OKLCH between five keyframes. NIGHT (sun below -12 degrees): glass bay, dusk-land, headlight and tail streaks, pools and open spots lit, reflections on the water. BLUE HOUR (-12 to 0): the bay goes blue-hour, and the lights switch on in a wave from the coast inland. GOLDEN (0 to +8): copper bay, warm land, and a sun glint stretched long toward the sun's azimuth (west at sunset, east at sunrise). DAY (+8 to +55): the shallows-to-channel water ramp, sand land with the Deco tints, boat wakes, and the beacon casting a crisp shadow away from the sun. HIGH SUN (above +55, around midday from roughly late February to late October in Miami): the shortest shadows and the most saturated shallows. The interface surfaces don't blend, because mid-tones go muddy: the board, bands and text flip between night and day tokens at -4 degrees with a 600ms crossfade. In November (the test trip) sunset is around 5:30pm, so evenings default to night mode.

graphicDevices: LIGHT TRAILS: long-exposure streaks. At night they are paired warm-white (headlight) and red (tail) streaks along real OSM roads, built from the existing traffic particles. In the interface the same stroke becomes the route between plan stops, the underline on the active filter and tab, and the progress line while Play runs. By day the device becomes boat wakes: a white V at the Kelvin wake half-angle (19.5 degrees) behind boats on the bay. Rule: a trail always means movement along a path, never a decorative swoosh.

THE BEACON: the pineapple period, lit. There is exactly one per view, and it marks the move. On the map it is a 14px pineapple glyph: at night with a 40px vertical light pillar and bloom, by day with a crisp ink shadow offset by the sun's azimuth. Within 200m of water it also drops a rippling reflection streak on the bay. It is the wordmark's period, the #1 pin, the Go button, and the loader (a pulsing period). Never scattered and never more than one; saved spots are plain ink or ink-night points.

TITLE CARDS: every move's name is set as a film title card in Science Gothic, with axes computed from its data, so each move gets its own type. The reference is Tom Kan's Enter the Void credits, where each credit is set for its person. The mapping uses real moves.json fields. energy 1-5 sets wght 380/500/640/780/900. secret 0/1/2 sets wdth 165/125/72, so the more hidden the move, the narrower its name. rainOk true (indoor proxy) sets CTRS 55; false sets 0. hm(best) at or after 22:00 or before 04:00 sets slnt -8 (a late-night lean); otherwise 0. category only chooses the wording of the credit line. Title cards replace the random-hash stickers as the photo stand-in and the collectible ('12 title cards collected').
signatureComponents: THE WINDOW (map stage; a rewrite of MiamiMap.svelte). A full-bleed canvas that is the only background in the app; on mobile, at rest, the UI never covers more than 54% of it. Static layer, rebuilt when the view changes: land fill, then water colored from a precomputed distance-from-coast field. To build the field, rasterize land once to a 512px offscreen canvas, run 3 box-blur passes, and read the result as 0-1 'depth'. Pass depth through the current phase's water ramp: shallows to channel by day, blue-hour to glass at night, copper at golden hour. Add roads by class, and by day the Deco tint by nearest neighborhood point at 35% alpha. Dynamic layer, every frame: traffic, glows of open moves (existing glow()), reflections, boats, the beacon, labels. Traffic: replace the per-car createRadialGradient with two pre-rendered 16px sprites (head, tail) plus short streak segments (length = speed x 0.25s), drawn with 'lighter' compositing at night. Budget: 600 particles on desktop, 280 on mobile. Bloom: draw the lights to a 1/8-size offscreen canvas and scale it back up with smoothing at 0.6 alpha (this works in Safari without ctx.filter). Frame budget: 6ms on an iPhone 12-class phone. If 3 consecutive frames take longer than 20ms, halve the particles and drop bloom. Night reflections: under each lit point within 200m of water, a 12-28px vertical gradient streak at 0.25 alpha, wobbling on a 3s sine. Neighborhood labels as signage: Science Gothic wdth 170, wght 300, 11px caps tracked 0.2em; stroke-only with a 6px glow at night, filled ink-day at 55% by day. Place them greedily with collision boxes so no two overlap (this fixes 'ALLAPATTAHDESIGN DISTRICT'). Truth line in Martian Mono at the map's corner: 'LIGHT FROM REAL OPENING HOURS · TRAFFIC AND BOATS ILLUSTRATIVE · POOLS FROM OSM'. Draw pools only if geo.mjs finds OSM leisure=swimming_pool features in the bounding box; otherwise skip them. Camera: flat top-down for all interaction. The cinematic tilt runs only during Lights On and fly-to: a wrapper div with perspective 1200px, rotateX(38deg), scale 1.25, over 900ms. Taps are disabled while tilted, and there is no tilt under reduced motion.

THE BEACON CARD (top of the sheet; a rewrite of NowView). It shows the single best move for the dial's hour, visible on first paint before any animation runs. From top to bottom: (1) a credit line in Martian Mono 11px caps, e.g. '6:42PM · ABOUT 12 MIN FROM BRICKELL · OPEN TILL 2AM · $$'; distance says 'about' and 'from <hood>' until the visitor shares a location. (2) The move name as its title card, 24-34px. (3) One sentence of 'the move' in Science Gothic body, 16px. (4) Two actions. 'Go' has a beacon fill and ink-day text, is 48px tall, and is a plain link to Apple Maps on iOS and Google Maps elsewhere. 'Another' is a ghost button that swaps to the next-ranked move while the beacon flies across the map drawing a light trail. Below the card, 'Also lit right now' lists compact 56px rows: Martian Mono time, title-card name at 18px, hood. Mobile first-paint budget at 390x844: map 388px, Sun Strip 40px, Beacon card at most 230px, one also-lit row at 56px, tab bar 64px plus safe area. That totals about 812px, so one complete answer and one alternative sit above the fold, which fixes critique #1. A secret (lean-in) move can be the Beacon: its name shows squeezed to wdth 50 and tinted flamingo, with 'Hold to lean in · 3 left this week'.

THE SUN STRIP (replaces Dial.svelte). A 40px strip covering 24 hours, painted hour by hour with the map's actual colors from the light model for today's date, not a generic gradient. It carries: sunrise and sunset ticks labeled in Martian Mono ('RISE 7:13 · SET 7:06'); a moon-phase glyph at night (new code: a simple synodic-month calculation, labeled 'calculated'); hourly rain bars from the baked weather, labeled 'forecast' or 'typical'; small ink ticks at the best hour of each saved move; and a playhead that is the sun disk by day and the moon by night, with a 44px hit area. Dragging scrubs time: the map re-lights every frame, the list re-ranks after 120ms with no movement, and the title cards morph to the new ranking. 'NOW' at the strip's right end snaps back to the present (replacing 'Back to now'). While you scrub, the top credit line reads 'SCRUBBING 1:30PM · REAL 4:42PM', so the two clocks never contradict each other the way the MIA chip and the dial do today. Keyboard: role=slider; left/right arrows move 15 min, PageUp/PageDown 1 hour, Home jumps to now; aria-valuetext reads like '6:42pm, golden hour'. A play button at the left end runs 24 hours in 20 seconds and stops on any input. On desktop the strip spans the bottom letterbox band; on mobile it forms the top edge of the sheet.

THE LONG EXPOSURE (the Plan's share image), plus the receipt, kept and restyled. 'Make the poster' renders a 1080x1350 offscreen canvas: the night map of the stay's area in the glass and blue-hour palette, each night's route drawn as additive light trails between stops (night 1 brightest), stops as small beacons and the peak event as the one Beacon. Type is set like a film poster: 'MIAMI' in Science Gothic caps at wdth 190, a credit line 'NOV 20 - 24, 2026', then wide credits listing each night's moves, with the receipt code (PINA-XXXXX) as the last credit. Await document.fonts.load before drawing; render in 400ms or less. The primary save path is an from a data URL that people long-press (mobile) or right-click to save. A Download link (canvas.toBlob plus a[download]) is only an enhancement: verify it works inside the sandboxed artifact before promising a Save button. The thermal receipt stays; it is the best existing component. Restyle it in Martian Mono, use beacon only once (on the code), and fix the empty days: planStay must fill daytime slots, and if nothing fits it prints one line in voice instead of a blank day.

layout.mobile: Phone first, 390x844. The top 46% (388px) is the Window, full-bleed. Over it sit the wordmark top-left (Science Gothic lowercase, wdth 125, wght 900, 30px, with the pineapple period at 0.42em in beacon, three times today's size) and a credit line top-right in Martian Mono 11px ('MIA 6:42PM · 86° · SET 7:06'). Both sit on a 64px scrim of glass at 55% along the top edge, which is there for contrast, not decoration. This replaces the pill chip and the recenter disc; recenter becomes a double-tap on the map. The hour's title card sits on the map's lower-left: at most 3 lines, caps, wdth fluid 110-130, 34-40px, ink-night with a 1px glass text-shadow over a 96px bottom scrim. Below the map is an opaque sheet (surface-night or paper, 20px radius on the top corners only, a 1px line, no blur). Its top edge is the 40px Sun Strip, followed by the Beacon card and one also-lit row, all above the fold. Dragging the sheet up opens the full list; the filters live there as one horizontally scrolling row of Martian Mono text toggles (ALL · CHILL · SOCIAL · WILD · RAIN-SAFE · CHEAP), with the active one marked by a light-trail underline. Dragging the sheet down gives the map 85%. Tab bar: Now, Plan, Wall, You, labeled in Science Gothic caps (wdth 150, 10px, tracked 0.12em); the active tab gets ink plus a 2px light-trail underline, since beacon is reserved for the move. Move, event and plan views raise the sheet to 88% but keep a 100px strip of map visible, so the beacon or route stays in view.
layout.desktop: 1440x900, cinematic. The Window fills the viewport between two solid letterbox bands (glass at night, paper by day). The top band (56px) holds the wordmark on the left, the tabs in the center (Science Gothic caps, tracked), and the live credit line on the right. The bottom band (72px) is the full-width Sun Strip with play and NOW. Between them the map frame is about 1.9:1. The board is a 420px opaque column flush to the left edge between the bands, with a hard 1px right rule, no radius and no blur, scrolling independently. It sits on the west, which is land, so Miami Beach and the bay stay visible on the right. It holds the Beacon card, the also-lit list and the filters. The hour's title card sits large over the map just right of the board (56-72px, wdth 160) and shrinks to a 2-line credit after the first interaction. Wall: the board widens to 860px with flyers in 3 columns, and hovering a flyer lights its venue on the map as the Beacon. Plan: the board holds the stay, and the map draws each night as light trails, with a night selector in the bottom band just above the Sun Strip. Move and event details replace the board's content (no floating card) with a back arrow, and the map flies to the place.

directions.motion: Tokens: --dur-ui 180ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) for press, toggle and hover. --dur-sheet 280ms cubic-bezier(.3,1.2,.4,1) for sheet snaps and card swaps. --dur-camera 900ms cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) for fly-to and tilt. --dur-title 600ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) for title cards settling into their axes. All interface motion stays at or under 300ms; camera moves and cinematic moments are separate, always skippable, and off under prefers-reduced-motion. Four signature motions. (1) Title-card settle: when the ranking changes or a card swaps, the name animates its own axes from wdth 200, wght 150 and opacity 0 to its settings, like a projected title coming into focus, over 600ms with a 40ms stagger per row. (2) Lights on at dusk: when the Sun Strip crosses -2 degrees, roads, pools and open spots switch on in a wave from the coast inland over 1.2s, staggered by the precomputed distance to the coast; at dawn the wave runs in reverse. (3) Fly-to: a 900ms camera ease to the selected move while a light trail draws from the previous beacon to the new one. (4) Lean-in: the existing 950ms hold, then a vignette closes on the card, the existing --lean variable drives the wordmark's Science Gothic width from 125 to 200 and back, and the hidden name opens from wdth 50 to its own width. Under reduced motion: traffic is frozen but still drawn as streaks, there is no tilt, no intro and no play loop, axis changes are instant, and crossfades last 150ms or less. Nothing flashes more than 3 times per second anywhere (WCAG 2.3.1): Enter the Void is a reference for its type, never for its strobe.

jawDropMoments.moment: LIGHTS ON: on the first open of each session, Miami switches on. Lasts 2.4s at most; any tap, scroll or key skips it.
jawDropMoments.how: A canvas-only overlay on the real map. The DOM (Beacon card and list) is fully rendered and interactive from frame 0, so it never blocks the answer. 0-0.8s: the coastline draws as a thin line of light from Key Biscayne northward (precompute the cumulative length of each coast polyline and use setLineDash([t*L, L])). 0.8-1.6s: roads switch on by distance from the coast (per-vertex distance precomputed once; alpha = smoothstep of t minus d). 1.6-2.4s: traffic streaks start, the Beacon drops onto the top move with its 40px light pillar, and the hero title card settles. If it is daytime in Miami, the same timeline runs as an exposure: color saturates in from an overexposed white frame, shallows first. Reduced motion shows the final frame only. Plays once per session (sessionStorage, wrapped in try/catch).

jawDropMoments.moment: SCRUB THE SUN: drag the strip and the whole city re-lights in real time. Continuous and user-driven, with no fixed duration.
jawDropMoments.how: The Sun Strip drives one phase value from the new solar-position function. It sets the water ramp, the land tint, the glint position (from azimuth), the traffic share (the existing hourly curve, labeled illustrative), pools switching on at dusk, and the glow of open moves via glow(). The list re-ranks after 120ms idle, and its title cards morph their axes instead of re-rendering. It stays within the frame budget because the static layer is cached in 24 phase buckets and only the dynamic layer redraws.

jawDropMoments.moment: LEAN IN AND IT WHISPERS BACK: hold a secret, the screen closes in on it, a synthesized 'psst', and a dark spot on the map lights up. About 1.4s in total.
jawDropMoments.how: Uses the existing 950ms hold-to-unlock in MoveCard. On unlock, a radial-gradient vignette closes on the card over 280ms, the wordmark stretches (wdth 125 to 200 to 125), the secret's title card opens from wdth 50 to its own width, and a beacon appears on the map in a place that was dark. Sound is off by default; one speaker toggle in You turns it on (stored in localStorage) and supplies the user gesture WebAudio needs. The synthesized 'psst': a 4ms high-passed click for 'p', then 300ms of white noise through a bandpass at 6.5kHz (Q 1.4, 15ms attack, 80ms release) for 'ss', then a 30ms burst at 3kHz for 't', with master gain 0.25. It never autoplays. Haptics use the existing navigator.vibrate([12,40,18]) where supported.

jawDropMoments.moment: THE LONG EXPOSURE: your whole stay as one night photograph you send to the group chat. Renders in 400ms or less, on demand.
jawDropMoments.how: A 1080x1350 offscreen canvas reusing the map's static layer in the night palette. Each night's route is an additive light trail: a 6px headlight core plus an 18px beacon or flamingo halo at 0.25 alpha with 'lighter' compositing. Stops are drawn as beacons and type is set like a film poster in Science Gothic (await document.fonts.load first). The output is an from a data URL for long-press saving; the download link ships only after a[download] is verified inside the artifact sandbox.

jawDropMoments.moment: A DAY MODE WORTH A SCREENSHOT: turquoise shallows, boat wakes, sun glint and the beacon's shadow. Always on when the sun is up.
jawDropMoments.how: The water ramp comes from the distance field (shallows #82E1E0 to channel #117FAA). Draw 12-20 boats on hand-drawn water polylines (Government Cut, the Intracoastal, the Rickenbacker to Key Biscayne), each a 3px white hull with a V wake at 19.5 degrees fading over 60px, labeled illustrative. Specular glint: a soft ellipse on the water at the anti-solar offset, sized by sun elevation and stretched along the azimuth at golden hour. The beacon casts a 50% ink shadow offset by (cos az, sin az) x 1/tan(elevation), clamped to 24px. Deco pastels are drawn on land by nearest neighborhood point at 35% alpha.

The random-hash stickers (Sticker.svelte) as each move's identity: replace with data-driven title cards. Keep the collecting mechanic, as title cards collected.

references: Marseille by La Phase 5: https://www.awwwards.com/sites/marseille-by-la-phase-5 (opened). Awwwards Site of the Day on 13 Mar 2021, scored 7.54/10. A city guide built on a real-time 3D map (WebGL, Three.js) with zoom-in transitions and 360-degree panoramas. psst. will be better because its map is lit by live data (real opening hours times the real sun) and it answers in one card on a phone. Marseille is a showcase you explore, not a tool for deciding where to go.

Mapbox Standard style light presets: https://docs.mapbox.com/map-styles/standard/guides (from search results; I did not open the page). Four fixed presets (dawn, day, dusk, night) that change color temperature and shadow direction. psst. goes further: light changes continuously with the sun's calculated elevation for the actual date, and the light carries meaning, because only what is open glows.

Enter the Void title sequence: https://fontsinuse.com/uses/61211/enter-the-void-title-sequence (opened). Tom Kan's 2009 credits for Gaspar Noé, with each credit set in its own typeface to reflect the person. psst. borrows the idea, not the look: each move's title card is computed from its data, and there is no strobe (the source page carries an epilepsy warning).

Bank Gothic in use: https://fontsinuse.com/typefaces/5475/bank-gothic (opened). Morris F. Benton for ATF, 1930-33, with 39 uses listed, including the Enter the Void sequence and also Grand Theft Auto III and GTA Online, which is why the GTA risk below is real.

Science Gothic specimen: https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Science+Gothic/about (opened). A 4-axis Bank Gothic revival with a lowercase and small caps added; the page says it is on more than 1,100 websites, so it is not overexposed.

The Infatuation Miami: https://www.theinfatuation.com/miami (opened; I read the computed styles). Black and white with a #0066F1 accent, set in National 2 / Narrow / Condensed, organized as editorial lists. psst. beats it on timing (this hour, this weather) and with an identity that doesn't look like a news site.

Places by Raya: https://www.placesbyraya.com (opened; computed styles). Black, white and warm greys, Antarctica Display with GT Flexa Mono, curated by 'luminaries' across many cities. It already uses the same display-plus-mono logic, so psst. has to win on color, light and Miami-only depth, not on the type pairing.

Pan American Seaplane Base and Terminal Building: https://www.nps.gov/articles/pan-american-seaplane-base-and-terminal-building.htm (opened). The concept proof: flying boats from Dinner Key from 1 Dec 1930, an Art Deco frieze of winged globes and rising suns, and the building has been Miami City Hall since 1954.

Fontshare ITF Free Font License v2.0, 17 Aug 2026: https://www.fontshare.com/licenses/itf-ffl (opened, rendered in a browser). It allows self-hosting via @font-face, but it counts subsetting and format conversion as prohibited modification and allows document embedding only where the font 'cannot be extracted'. Excluded for this artifact.

Not useful or not reached: godly.website now redirects to recent.design, which has no searchable archive; siteinspire's search returned only its latest feed; Mobbin needs a login, so I didn't check it. Typewolf has no Bank Gothic page (404), and its Google Fonts roundup lists neither Science Gothic nor Martian Mono, a weak sign that neither is overused.
antiTemplateChecks: 1 Font check: PASS. Science Gothic and Martian Mono; neither is on the template-default list (Inter, Geist, Roboto, Poppins, Montserrat, Space Grotesk, Space Mono). Science Gothic was added to Google Fonts on 19 Nov 2025 (per its metadata) and its page says it is on 1,100+ sites. Caveat: it shares Bank Gothic's lineage with GTA's interface (see risks).

2 Accent check: PASS WITH CAVEAT. Beacon #FFB127 is not used by The Infatuation (#0066F1), Places by Raya (no accent), DICE (#F2EF1D) or Bumble (#FFF500), all checked live. The nearest famous amber is Amazon orange (commonly cited as #FF9900, not verified live), which is outside the category and about 10 degrees redder in hue. The current #FFC53D fails as an owned color because it marks four different things.

3 Layout check: PASS. This is not the centered-hero, three-cards, logo-row, pricing stack. It is one full-bleed map stage, an opaque board and a time strip, and the first thing on screen is a single answer (the Beacon card).

4 Device check: PASS WITH CAVEAT, UNTESTED, because no mockup exists yet. With the logo covered, light trails and boat wakes, a single amber beacon and wide title cards over a lit Miami coastline should identify psst. But neon over a dark city is a genre, so the day mode (turquoise shallows, wakes, Deco tints) carries more of the ownership and must be built to the same standard. Re-run this check on the first build.

5 Decoration check: PASS WITH CAVEAT. Glass blur, pills and generic glow blobs are cut, and every remaining glow is light that is really on at that hour (open spots from opening hours, traffic by hour, pools from OSM). Bloom and neon labels are glow by definition, so the rule is: glow only on things that are lit in reality at that hour, and shadows only from the sun's actual azimuth.

6 Voice check: PASS. The hero ('Sun's gone at 7:06. Be on the water by 6:50.'), the error ('Can't see you from up here. Pick a neighborhood and I'll point.') and the confirmation ('Saved. It'll light up on your map when it's the right hour.') read as the same timed, specific whisper. The risk is airport puns creeping in; they are on the never list.

7 Concept check: PASS. (a) Beacon amber is the one light the friend points at, and it is the pineapple (hospitality) period. (b) Title cards show the city like a film seen from the window, with axes taken from each move's own data. (c) The Sun Strip is the window's light: one drag re-lights the whole city from the sun's real position.
risks: GTA VI launches 19 Nov 2026 (the date Take-Two confirmed, per press coverage including PCWorld), the day before the test trip (Nov 20-24), and it is set in a Miami stand-in. Neon night-time Miami plus a Bank Gothic revival can read as fan art that week. Mitigation: no pink-orange-purple sunset gradient anywhere, beacon amber rather than pink as the hero color, lowercase-led titles with caps only for credits, and a day mode as strong as the night. If the founder still reads it as GTA, swap the display face to Sprat (the fallback above).

Metaphor creep: the founder killed the hotel metaphor as slop. Night Flight must stay in camera, light and type: no boarding passes, departure boards, seat maps, gates or 'now boarding' copy. Check every string against the voice never-list.

Phone performance: particles, bloom and reflections can drop a mid-range Android below 30fps. The budgets and auto-degrade rules are specified, but test on a real mid-range phone, not only desktop Chrome.

Real or labeled: the traffic and boats are illustrative (the hourly traffic curve is a typical pattern, not live), pools must come from OSM or not be drawn, and drive times are estimates. The map's truth line has to say so, or the build breaks the brief's honesty rule.
Night can still read as a 'moody dark template' if the colored lights (pool, flamingo, headlight, tail) and the day mode are not built to spec. The brief asks for colorful and playful.
Legibility of title cards over a lit map: they need the specified scrims, plus a contrast check over the brightest region of the map in each light phase.
Science Gothic as a body face: it was readable at 16px and wdth 95 in my render, but it feels mechanical. If people struggle in a test, adding a quiet text face would break the two-family rule.

Font weight: the Science Gothic Latin file is 156KB and Martian Mono's is 38KB (about 195KB together). Use display=swap with size-adjusted Arial fallbacks, and request only the axes in use (drop slnt if the late-night lean is cut in review).
Process: this pass collapses the skill's step-by-step approvals into one deliverable. Get the founder's yes on concept, then type, then color before build.

Review harness: the r0 shots were taken with reduced motion and probably hit the hash-navigation artifact. The next review needs motion captures (a 10s recording of Lights On and a sun scrub), or the motion work won't be judged at all.

directions.name: Tear Here: today's Miami as a pad of tear-off moves
directions.oneLine: psst. hands you today's Miami as a short pad of tear-off tickets, each one a move that is good for a specific hour, on a screen painted the color of Miami's sky right now; you tear off the ones you'll do, and the stubs you keep become your collection.
critiqueOfCurrent: mobile-now-day.png: the first viewport is about 40% grey map and 60% clock, controls, headline and weather (1:30pm, SCRUBBING · DAYLIGHT, Back to now / Play the day, the 24h pill). Not one move is visible above the tab bar; the filter chips are cut off at the fold. The product's one job, handing you the move, is missing from the first screen. desktop-now-day.png is the same problem with a pale teal and grey map that reads as a Google Maps clone, monospace labels collide (ALLAPATTAHDESIGN DISTRICT) and the screen shows two dots.

mobile-now-golden.png and desktop-now-golden.png: 'golden hour' renders the map as a murky grey-green wash, the least golden screen in the set. The sky-lit lighting is supposed to be the differentiator, and at the most photogenic hour of the Miami day the only warm thing on screen is the copy ('Face west and stop talking').

desktop-move.png, desktop-event.png, desktop-plan.png, desktop-wall.png, desktop-you.png: on every desktop view except Now the map disappears and about 1,000px of empty navy sits to the right of a 440px glass panel. This is a phone sheet stretched across a monitor. desktop-you.png also puts a light panel on the dark void with a ghosted, unreadable logo.

mobile-plan-scrolled.png and desktop-receipt.png: the planner breaks the brand promise. 'The 3:05 cafecito' is scheduled at 5:06pm under SUNSET, 'Sunrise swim off Virginia Key' at 6:15pm under DINNER, Saturday has one stop (a locked secret) and doesn't include John Summit night 2, Sunday to Tuesday have none, and the receipt prints 'COST less than you think'. A friend who knows Miami would never send you on a sunrise swim at dinner, so this is a failure of taste, not only a bug.

mobile-move.png (r0) and shots/r1-data/mobile-move.png: the screenshot named 'move' never shows a move. It shows the Now list at 10pm, and in the real-data version the first two rows are blurred locked secrets ('Press and hold to lean in · 3 left this week'). The main list is mostly content you can't read, and the core object, one move, has no screen of its own on mobile.

mobile-wall.png and mobile-event.png: the generated riso flyers are the most distinctive asset, but they break words mid-word (THUNDE/RCAT, COUNTR/Y, NEW ROAD), squeeze long bills ('ÂME (DJ), HARDT ANTOINE & MACEO PLEX') into condensed caps, and print 'FRI OCT 2' twice on one flyer. The Andy Stott flyer is a red circle on yellow dots. They read as auto-generated, not as found on a Calle Ocho pole.

mobile-now-night.png and desktop-now-night.png: the night skin is the stock template, purple-navy (#0B0820) with a cyan glow coastline, orange glow roads, a glass panel and outline pills. It could be any DJ or crypto app. Developer language ('SCRUBBING · AFTER DARK', 'Back to now', 'Play the day') sits where the hero line should be.

All screens: the brand barely shows. The wordmark is 32–40px with a pineapple about 8px tall. The main accent --sun #FFC53D is effectively Bumble's yellow (#FFC629), and the move rows are generic list UI (5-dot energy pips, $$$, teal/pink 'lowkey'/'lean in' pills). The six-pill filter row (Everything, Chill, Social, Wild, Rain-safe, Cheap) wraps to two lines on mobile-now-night.png and pushes the moves further down. Nobody would screenshot any of this to send to a friend.
directions.concept: Concept sentence: "The friend who knows Miami tears you a ticket for the right hour." How it extends 'the friend who knows Miami': a friend doesn't hand you a map with 400 pins. They lean over at 3:05 and slip you one thing, with the time and exactly what to order. A ticket stub is the physical form of that tip. It has a valid window (the hour), an admission instruction (the move), a serial number (No. 012 of 43, so it's collectible) and a perforation, which makes keeping it a gesture. Proof it isn't decoration: the name is the whisper before a tip, and the pineapple period (hospitality) becomes the sun on the time track. The Wall already says 'Tear one off' and the Receipt already prints plans, so the stub turns what the product already has into one object. Tilt Warp, the display face, is described in its repo as resembling 'peeling vinyl stickers' and is built from storefront sign painting. The daily ritual: a fresh pad every morning (5–7 stubs ordered by hour). One sealed secret drops daily at 3:05pm, Miami's cafecito hour and its 305 area code. Every Thursday at 3:05pm the weekend pad drops for locals. Visitors get the Strip, their stay as a roll of stubs. Why it beats Google Maps in the first 5 seconds. At 0.0s the screen is the flat color of Miami's sky this minute (pool blue at 3pm, mamey at golden hour, bay ink at night), with the hour in 76px sign lettering. At 0.6s the pad lands with one stub on top for right now: 'The 3:05 cafecito at Las Olas' sidewalk window · good till 8pm · 12 min · walk up to the ventanita, order a cafecito, take a Cuban cut extra thin to the beach'. At 1.5s the next stub peeks out and 'Later today' shows the shape of the day. By 5s you've decided, or swiped. Google Maps at 5s shows a grey map, a blue dot and an empty search bar: it answers 'where' only after you already know 'what'. psst. answers what, when, why and how before you ask, and Maps is still one tap away on every stub.

voice.register: A Miami friend texting from the ventanita: specific, warm, a little conspiratorial, deadpan about tourist traps. Short imperative sentences that carry exact details (the time, what to order, which door, cash or card). Spanish only where Miami already uses it (cafecito, colada, ventanita, pastelito), never as a costume. Jokes: at most one dry aside per screen, always attached to a real fact ('Face west. Stop talking.'). Never puns on Miami Vice, flamingos or 'vibes', and no exclamation marks.
voice.errorLine: Closed today and nobody told us. Here's where the regulars went instead.
voice.receiptLine: Kept. No. 012 is yours. Go before 8.

typography.role: Display, 'the sign': the hour, move titles, wordmark, section heads. 20px and up only.
typography.family: Tilt Warp (Andy Clymer, Google Fonts), variable axes XROT and YROT, each -45 to 45
typography.license: SIL Open Font License 1.1, as stated in the repo. Commercial use is allowed. The OFL allows embedding, and documents made with the font are not bound by the license. Delivery: through the CSP-allowed Google Fonts stylesheet (css2?family=Tilt+Warp:XROT,YROT@-45..45,-45..45). I measured the latin woff2 at 68 KB with both axes intact, so no base64 is needed. If it ever has to be inlined, base64 the unmodified woff2 and keep the copyright and OFL notice in a CSS comment.
typography.why: It comes from storefront sign painting, and the repo describes Warp as resembling peeling vinyl stickers, which is exactly the material of a collectible stub. Its rotation axes put the psst. lean-in inside the font: on press-and-hold the title rotates toward you (font-variation-settings 'XROT' 0,'YROT' -28). I tested it at real sizes on a stub: legible at 20px ('Walk in for a frozen martini when Sunny's opens'), with accents (Máximo Gómez), strong numerals at 76–132px (digits are proportional, with no tnum; the hour sets each digit in a fixed 0.62em cell). Tokens: --type-hour 76px mobile / 132px desktop, line-height .92, tracking -0.01em, the 'pm' at .36em. --type-title 30px/1.02 on stubs (max 4 lines, text-wrap: balance). --type-section 22px/1.1. Sentence case only, never all caps, never below 20px. It replaces Anybody.

typography.role: Voice and measure: the friend's note, UI body, and the ticket printer (every time, price, temperature, serial and label)
typography.family: Recursive (Arrow Type / Stephen Nixon, Google Fonts), axes used: wght, CASL, MONO
typography.license: SIL Open Font License 1.1, per the repo. Commercial use and embedding are allowed. Delivery: Google Fonts stylesheet css2?family=Recursive:wght,CASL,MONO@400..800,0..1,0..1, measured at 142 KB latin woff2 as a variable font. Don't request slnt or CRSV, because the full five-axis file is 305 KB, too heavy for phones on 4G. Set MONO and CASL with font-variation-settings in caps, per the repo's guidance.
typography.why: One family gives three voices through its axes, and each maps to a role in the concept. The friend's handwriting: CASL 1, MONO 0, weight 500, 17px/1.36, used only for the move's note (moves.json 'theMove'). Quiet UI: CASL 0, MONO 0, weights 450/650, 15–16px/1.45. The ticket printer: MONO 1, CASL 0, weight 500, 11–13px, uppercase, +0.07em tracking. Mono digits are tabular by construction, so '10:00pm' never jitters while you scrub. Tested at 12px ('OPEN 08:00–05:00 · 86°/80° · RAIN 28%'). It replaces both Figtree and DM Mono, so the system has two families plus one rationed cut.

typography.role: Night hour only, exactly one element: the signs come on after sunset
typography.family: Tilt Neon (Andy Clymer, Google Fonts), same skeleton as Tilt Warp
typography.license: SIL Open Font License 1.1, per the repo. Load it with the Google Fonts text subset (css2?family=Tilt+Neon:XROT,YROT@-45..45,-45..45&text=0123456789:apm). I measured that at 21.5 KB, against 166 KB for the full latin file.
typography.why: It's built like neon tube lettering on the same letter model as Tilt Warp. When the sky passes sunset, the hour in the sky band switches from Warp (painted vinyl) to Neon (lit tube), as Ocean Drive's signs do. Color neon oklch(0.85 0.09 50) #FFBD99 with text-shadow 0 0 14px mamey/70%. It is limited to that one element so it never slides into the South Beach neon cliché, and it's the only glow in the system.

tokens.name: --line

tokens.name: --mamey (owned accent)
