color.ownedAccent: Mamey, #F37F5F / oklch(0.72 0.15 36), a salmon-coral named for the mamey batido. Rule: mamey means NOW. It marks the present moment everywhere (live dot, now-marker, pineapple-sun) and appears once per view, except during golden hour, when the whole sky field warms to --sky-golden by design.
color.nearestCompetitorColor: Partiful's homepage orange #FE8207 (scraped from partiful.com) is the nearest, at ΔE_OK 0.061. Mamey is 18° pinker in hue (36 vs 54), lower in chroma (0.15 vs 0.18) and reads salmon-coral rather than traffic-cone orange, and Partiful's core identity is purple-to-pink gradients with black. Next are the Miami Dolphins orange #FC4C02 (0.093) and Google Maps red #EA4335 (about 0.10, hue 29, more saturated). For the record, the current accent #FFC53D sits on top of Bumble's #FFC629 and Google Maps' yellow #FBBC04, which is why it goes.
color.dayNight: The background is a flat field the color of the actual Miami sky for the scrubbed hour. It's computed from sunFor(date) and keyed to the seven --sky stops above, with each boundary interpolated in OKLab over 30 minutes; there's no tween while dragging, and a 900ms ease when following live time. The MiamiMap canvas draws behind it tone-on-tone: water is the sky color, land is color-mix(in oklch, sky 62%, --paper) by day (sun-bleached) and sky-night +0.05 L at night, the coast is a 1.2px ink hairline at 45%, major roads 1.6px ink at 22%, primary roads 1px ink at 10%. There are no labels and no glow by day. After sunset the major roads carry the existing traffic particles and the hour switches to Tilt Neon. Stubs stay paper in every state, so contrast never depends on the time. Text on a sky is always --ink (light skies) or --paper (dusk and night), never --muted.

graphicDevices: The perforation: a 2px dashed line (6px dash, 6px gap, --line) inside a 22px band, with 10px half-moon notches cut into both edges (CSS mask with two radial gradients, so the sky shows through). Appears on every stub, between days on the Strip, on the tear-off tabs added to the foot of Wall flyers, and in share images. Never as a list divider, a settings separator or ornamental border.

The sky field: a flat, full-bleed color of Miami's real sky at the scrubbed hour, with the OSM coastline drawn tone-on-tone underneath. It is the page background on every surface. Never a decorative gradient, never on a card, never blurred glass.

Die-cut sticker emblems: the existing Sticker.svelte art (shape by category, palette by id hash) wrapped in a 3px --paper die-cut border with a drop shadow (0 4px 3px rgba(5,39,57,.3)). They're the art on stubs, the pins on the map (28–36px) and the slots in the Book. Never used as UI icons; tabs are text-only.
The rubber stamp: Recursive Mono caps 10.5px inside a 2px border, radius 6, rotated -8°, 85% opacity, in the move's deep ink. Used only for states: GOOD NOW, TOMORROW, KEPT, WENT 10.02, HOOD DONE.

The pineapple-sun: the period of the psst. wordmark (0.24em mamey circle) is the same object as the sun on the time track. On the Now screen it visibly travels from the wordmark to the track on first load, and at 3:05pm it turns into a small cafecito cup.
signatureComponents: THE STUB (one move; events use the same object). Size 358×~470 on mobile (full width minus 16px gutters), 400×~500 on desktop. Card stock --paper, radius 4px with 9px concave corner notches (CSS mask: four radial-gradient circles, 9px, at the corners). Shadow 0 1px 0 rgba(5,39,57,.06), 0 18px 28px -16px rgba(5,39,57,.45), allowed because a stub physically sits on the sky. Main body, padding 14/16: (1) a top row in Recursive Mono 11.5px caps: left '● GOOD NOW · TILL 8PM' (the dot is mamey with a 2px ink ring, shown only when now is inside an open window; otherwise 'BEST 10PM · OPENS 5PM'), right the travel time ('12 MIN' walk from geolocation, labeled 'FROM BRICKELL' when location is denied). (2) The hour bar: 12px tall, radius 6, track oklch(0.93 0.012 80). Today's open windows from moves.json 'windows' are filled with color-mix(mamey 55%, paper), the best-hour tick is 2px --ink, and the now marker is 4px mamey with a 2px paper halo. (3) The emblem: Sticker art at 88px, top right (right 12, top 38), rotated by id hash (-10° to 10°), with die-cut border. (4) The title in Tilt Warp 30/1.02, right margin 92px, max 4 lines. (5) The note ('theMove') in Recursive CASL 1, weight 500, 17/1.36, max 4 lines, then 'more' (flip). (6) A meta row in Mono 11.5px: hood · cost as '$' glyphs · one energy word (1–2 low-key, 3 lively, 4–5 loud) · 'rain ok' or 'skip if raining'. Then the perforation. The tear-off (84px) is tinted color-mix(move ink 16%, paper): on the left 'MOVE NO.' (Mono 10.5px) over a serial '012/043' in Tilt Warp 30px in the move's deep ink (the serial is the move's stable index in curated order, so it's real). On the right a 44px ink pill 'Hold to tear' (Recursive 650 15px). A rubber stamp sits on the perforation, and vertical microtext down the right edge reads 'ADMIT ONE · FRI 10.02' (writing-mode vertical-rl, Mono 9.5px, .2em). The back (tap to flip, rotateY 180°, 240ms): 'How to get in' (getIn), the 24h bar with 12am/6am/noon/6pm labels, the 'why' line, the address, buttons 'Show me where' / Apple Maps / Google Maps, and 'Checked Oct 2 · sources' in Mono. States: now; later (no live dot, stamp TOMORROW or BEST 10PM); sealed (see the Pad); kept (stamp KEPT, the tear-off stays in your Book); went (a 14px hole punched through the tear-off plus a WENT 10.02 stamp). An event stub swaps the emblem and title for the riso Flyer art cropped 4:3 across the top half, so there's one object system. Fix the Flyer: no mid-word breaks (hyphens: manual; shrink to fit by measuring line widths, then 2 lines max), and print the date once.

THE PAD ON THE SKY (Today, the home screen). Mobile, top to bottom: (1) the wordmark (Tilt Warp 30px + pineapple period) and, on the right, 'FRI OCT 2 · 86° · SET 7:06' (Mono). (2) The hour, Tilt Warp 76px (Tilt Neon after sunset). (3) The time track: a 2px line (ink at 35%) across the full width, with the pineapple-sun (18px mamey, 2px ink ring; a crescent at night) at hour/24. Drag to scrub in 15-minute steps with pointer capture; arrow keys move 15 min, PgUp/PgDn 1h, Home returns to now; tapping the hour also returns to now. A 'Back to now' Mono chip shows only when you're more than 30 min away. This replaces Dial.svelte, its gradient pill and both buttons. (4) The lede in Recursive CASL 1, weight 600, 18px ('psst. It's cafecito o'clock.'), from the existing line() table rewritten in voice. (5) The pad: the top stub plus two backs peeking 8px below, rotated +2.2° and -1.4°. Swipe left for the next stub (it leaves rotating -8°), swipe right for the previous, tap to flip, hold the tear-off for 650ms or drag it down more than 60px to tear. Order is rankNow() for the current hour, at most 7 stubs per pad, at most one sealed secret and never in positions 1–2. (6) 'Later today': a horizontal row of 118×76 mini stubs (paper, Mono time + Recursive 600 13px title); tapping one scrubs the hour to that stub's best time. (7) Tabs: Today · Wall · Trip · Book, text only, with an ink pill on the active tab. The six-chip filter row is gone. When the pad holds more than 4 stubs, one segmented control 'Low-key | Loud' appears under the lede, and rain-safe applies automatically when rainAt() is 50% or more, with a one-line note. The 3:05 drop: from 15:05 Miami time, position 3 of the pad is a sealed stub. It's an ink envelope with a mamey wax-seal dot, the hood name and a one-line clue in Recursive CASL 1 ('Brickell. Ring twice.'). Holding it 950ms spends a lean (3 a week) and opens it. Every Thursday at 15:05 the pad header becomes 'This weekend' and holds Friday to Sunday's stubs plus Wall events.

THE BOOK (replaces You). An album with one page per neighborhood group: Little Havana · Brickell/Downtown · Wynwood/Edgewater/Allapattah · Design District/Little River/Little Haiti/MiMo · South/Mid/North Beach · Coral Gables/Coconut Grove · Key Biscayne/Virginia Key · South Dade. Each page has the hood name in Tilt Warp 34px, a 100%-width tone-on-tone mini map cropped to the hood (same field renderer, with sticker pins), and a two-column grid of numbered slots. An empty slot is a dashed outline of its emblem shape, plus the serial and a clue in Recursive CASL 1 ('No. 027 · ring twice'). A kept slot is the emblem sticker slapped in at ±8° (520ms spring). A went slot adds a hole punch and a WENT 10.02 stamp. When every slot on a page is 'went', a HOOD DONE stamp lands and that hood's sealed secret opens for free. Header: '12 kept · 5 went · 3 leans left this week' (Mono), with leans refilling Monday at 15:05. Redeeming a friend's PINA code moves here as a small ticket-shaped input. State lives in localStorage with try/catch, and the page renders empty-but-whole without it. The habit loop is Beli's 'been' count without the leaderboard: you complete Miami, you don't compete for it.

THE STRIP (Trip; the visitor plan, test case Nov 20–24, 2026, John Summit at Kaseya Center). The stay renders as a roll of stubs, vertical on mobile and horizontal on desktop, with one perforated band per day. The day header is in Mono: 'FRI NOV 20 · 79° TYPICAL · SUNSET 5:30'. Hard rules in the planner, unit-tested: a move can only sit inside its open 'windows' on that weekday, within ±90 min of its 'best' unless the user drags it. Slot labels come from the slot's time (morning / lunch / 3:05 / golden / dinner / late), never the reverse, so 'Sunrise swim' can't land at DINNER. Each day gets 2–4 stops with no empty days, and anchor events (John Summit night 1 and night 2) appear as event stubs with their flyer. Arrival and departure times (landing 3pm, flight out 1pm) clip the first and last days. Energy uses the same 'Low-key | Loud' control. Share: 'Send the strip' draws a 1080×1920 PNG on canvas (after document.fonts.ready; stubs, stickers, perforations and the PINA code) and hands it to navigator.share({files}) or a download link. 'Copy for the group chat' keeps the Receipt's plain-text format as a fallback. The separate Receipt modal goes away, and its thermal-printer voice lives on in the Mono printing on every stub.

layout.mobile: 390×844 first. There are no sheets, drag handles or glass. The page is the sky field (with the map tone-on-tone behind it), and content sits directly on it. Today, from the top: safe-area + 12px, then the wordmark row (44px), the hour (76px Tilt Warp, about 70px tall), the track (22px), the lede (18px CASL 1), the pad (top stub about 470px plus 16px of stack peek), 'Later today' mini stubs (76px, horizontal scroll with 16px gutters), and the tab bar (64px + safe area, paper with ink text, not glass). At 390×844 with no browser chrome the whole top stub, its title, note and 'Hold to tear' fit without scrolling (about 818px total, checked in a scratch mock). When innerHeight is under 800 (iOS safe areas, Safari bars), the note clamps to 3 lines and 'Later today' scrolls below the fold. The stub's tear button must never be cut off. Tapping 'Show me where' turns Today into the map. The map goes interactive full-screen with the stub collapsed to its sticker on the venue, and a 'Back to the pad' chip at the bottom. Wall: a two-column masonry of flyers on the sky field. Each flyer gets three tear-off tabs at its foot that save the event as a stub; titles never break mid-word. Trip: the Strip, vertical, days separated by perforations. Book: one neighborhood page per screen, swipe horizontally between pages like an album. 16px side gutters everywhere and no horizontal page scroll except the deliberate mini-stub row.
layout.desktop: 1440×900. The sky field and the interactive tone-on-tone MiamiMap fill the entire viewport. There is never an empty navy void. Left column, 470px wide, padding 28/32: the wordmark (40px), the hour (132px Tilt Warp), the track, the lede, then the pad (400px stub). The rest of the width is the live map, framed with the stub column as its left inset. Every stub in today's pad is also pinned on the map as its die-cut sticker at its venue, with a Mono time label. Hovering a sticker lifts the matching stub (translateY -6px), hovering a stub pulses its sticker, and the 'Later today' row runs along the bottom of the map as a horizontal strip of mini stubs. Trip: the Strip runs horizontally across the bottom 300px of the map with one column per day, and you drag a stub from the pad into a day slot to schedule it (pointer events, with a keyboard alternative 'Add to Fri'). Wall: flyers cover the right side as a pasted wall (CSS columns, ±2° rotation, paper tabs), with the map dimmed to 12% beneath. Book: a two-page album spread centered over the map. Keyboard: Tab order is pad, then map stickers, then Later strip; Enter flips, T tears, arrows scrub.

directions.motion: Motion means paper and light, nothing else. Tokens: --t-tap 120ms ease-out (press scale .98, stamps appearing); --t-ui 240ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) (flip, swipe to next, tab change, map pan start); --t-paper 520ms cubic-bezier(.3,1.35,.5,1) (sticker slap into the Book, stub landing on the pad). --t-paper is the only motion over 300ms and it never blocks input. Sky color changes immediately while scrubbing and eases over 900ms when following live time. The stack deal on scrub staggers 30ms per stub. Sound is off by default (toggle in the Book) and uses WebAudio only after a user gesture; haptics are navigator.vibrate where supported, so Android only, with visuals carrying it on iOS. Under prefers-reduced-motion there is no rotation, axis tilt, flight, flicker or chads: a tear becomes a 120ms crossfade plus the KEPT stamp, flips become crossfades, the sky changes instantly, font axes stay at 0, and the pineapple doesn't travel. Everything stays fully keyboard-operable (hold-to-tear equals Enter, then confirm).

jawDropMoments.moment: Tear here: you pull the stub off the pad and it tears along the perforation.
jawDropMoments.how: In Svelte 5, the stub is two layers: main body and tear-off. On pointerdown over the tear-off, start a 650ms progress (or track drag distance up to 60px). Draw the torn edge as an SVG path along the perforation with jagged vertices seeded by the move id (mulberry32), revealing it left to right by progress, and update a clip-path: polygon() on both layers so the paper separates along it. At each hole the edge passes (every 12px), play a 25ms band-passed noise burst through WebAudio (white-noise AudioBuffer → BiquadFilter bandpass 2.2–3.4kHz, randomized → GainNode envelope) and call navigator.vibrate(4) where supported. On completion the main body falls away (translateY 40px, rotate -6°, opacity 0, 240ms), the tear-off rotates upright, a KEPT stamp lands (120ms scale 1.3 to 1), then the tear-off flies FLIP-style into the Book tab (getBoundingClientRect to the tab, 520ms paper easing) and the tab's counter bumps +1. Reduced motion: a 120ms crossfade and the stamp.

jawDropMoments.moment: The signs come on: scrub past sunset and Miami lights up.
jawDropMoments.how: In the sky-field $effect, when daylight(hour) crosses the sunset threshold, swap the hour's font-family from Tilt Warp to Tilt Neon with a two-frame flicker (keyframes opacity 1, .25, 1, .4, 1 over 180ms), add text-shadow 0 0 14px mamey/70%, cross-fade the field to --sky-dusk then --sky-night, and in MiamiMap.svelte switch the buildCache() mode from 'day' to 'field-night' (land sky-night +0.05 L, major roads redrawn as warm light at oklch(0.80 0.12 60 / .6), traffic particles on, using the existing CARS loop). With sound on, a 400ms hum: two OscillatorNodes at 60Hz and 120Hz at -36dB with a 30ms attack. Scrubbing back before sunset reverses it without the flicker.

jawDropMoments.moment: Lean in: hold a sealed stub and the letters physically lean toward you.
jawDropMoments.how: Tilt Warp's variable axes: during the 950ms hold, animate font-variation-settings from 'XROT' 0,'YROT' 0 to 'XROT' 0,'YROT' -28 with requestAnimationFrame driving a CSS custom property (--yrot) read in font-variation-settings: 'YROT' var(--yrot). The stub scales to 1.03, the sky field dims 15% (an overlay at --ink 15%), and the hidden title un-blurs letter by letter (each span's filter: blur(6px) to 0 staggered by index × progress). The existing lean ring on the tear-off fills as a conic-gradient. On iOS, after a tap, ask DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission(), then the hour headline tilts with the phone (YROT = clamp(beta - 45, -20, 20)). Without permission, pointer position drives it.

jawDropMoments.moment: Show me where: the stub folds into its sticker and slaps onto the map at the exact venue.
jawDropMoments.how: FLIP the stub's emblem element to the venue's screen point from MiamiMap's project() and toScreen() (export them from the component). The stub body scales into the emblem: border-radius to 50%, width and height to 36px, 240ms. Meanwhile the map view tweens (view.cx, view.cy, view.s) from the city fit to the venue at about 4× in 600ms with an ease-in-out, and the canvas re-renders each frame from the cached field layer. On arrival the sticker does a squash and stretch (scale 1.25/.8 to 1, 520ms paper easing), then a dotted walking line (Canvas setLineDash [2,6], ink 60%) draws from the user's geolocation, or from the previous stub on the day, with lineDashOffset animated, and a Mono label '12 MIN' at the midpoint. 'Back to the pad' reverses it.

jawDropMoments.moment: 3:05 drop: at cafecito o'clock the pineapple turns into a cup and a sealed envelope slides into the pad.
jawDropMoments.how: An $effect on app.now: when Miami time is 15:05–15:15 (miamiNow() already exists), morph the wordmark's pineapple SVG into a cafecito cup by cross-fading two inline SVGs, with steam drawn from the coffee Sticker's three wavy paths animated via stroke-dashoffset. Insert the day's sealed secret, chosen deterministically from the 8 secret=2 moves by day-of-year, at pad position 3 with a 520ms slide-and-settle. Outside the window it appears as a quiet sealed stub, so the ritual still works for people who open later. On Thursdays the same moment flips the pad header to 'This weekend'.

jawDropMoments.moment: Scrub the sky: drag the pineapple-sun and the whole city recolors, with the stubs reshuffling like a dealer's hand.
jawDropMoments.how: The track handler sets app.hour (reuse Dial.svelte's setFrom and key logic). skyColor(hour) interpolates the seven OKLCH stops in OKLab (small inline lerp, no library) and writes --sky on .app, which repaints the CSS background and triggers MiamiMap's cache rebuild only when the colour changes by more than ΔE 0.01. Use Svelte 5 keyed {#each} with animate:flip plus in:fly (y 12, rotate ±2 via a custom transition, 30ms stagger) so stubs re-deal as rankNow() changes. Tilt Warp digits are proportional (measured advance widths 377–646 units, no tnum feature), so render each digit of the hour in its own inline-block 0.62em wide, text-align center, so the hour never jitters while scrubbing.

jawDropMoments.moment: Send the stub: one tap turns a move into a share card a friend actually opens.
jawDropMoments.how: Canvas 1080×1350, after await document.fonts.ready: fill the current --sky, draw the tone-on-tone coastline crop around the venue (reuse MiamiMap's fillSet/strokeSet against an offscreen canvas), then the stub: paper rect with 9px corner notches (arc cut-outs via destination-out), title with ctx.font = "84px 'Tilt Warp'", note with ctx.font = "500 40px Recursive" (canvas cannot set the CASL/MONO axes, so the share card uses Recursive's default linear instance; acceptable), Mono-style serial drawn with ctx.letterSpacing = '4px', the perforation as a dashed line plus two destination-out half circles, and the sticker by serializing the Sticker SVG to a Blob URL and ctx.drawImage. Footer: 'psst. Miami · good 3:05–8pm Fri Oct 2'. canvas.toBlob → navigator.canShare?.({files}) ? navigator.share({files, text}) : an <a download='psst-012.png'> fallback (blob URL).

The dark-by-default night palette (#0B0820 purple-navy, cyan glow coastline, orange glow roads, the gradient dial pill). Night is now --sky-night with paper stubs and one neon hour.

The six-chip filter row (Everything, Chill, Social, Wild, Rain-safe, Cheap). It's replaced by one 'Low-key | Loud' control shown only when the pad has more than 4 stubs, plus automatic rain-safe.
The --sun #FFC53D button yellow (Bumble's #FFC629). Primary buttons are --ink pills.
Anybody, Figtree and DM Mono, replaced by Tilt Warp + Recursive (+ a Tilt Neon digits subset).

The 5-dot energy pips, the 'lowkey' and 'lean in' pill tags, and the generic list rows (MoveCard.svelte as a row). Every move is a stub; lists are mini stubs.
The mobile bottom sheet and its drag handle (App.svelte .panel/.handle/full logic).
The separate Receipt modal and filler like 'COST less than you think'. Its text export survives as 'Copy for the group chat' on the Strip.

The 1.9s intro splash with the tagline 'Miami, from the people who'd never tell you.' The pineapple-sun travelling from the wordmark to the track is the intro, about 600ms, and skipped under reduced motion.
The 'You' tab name and its empty-state copy 'Your sticker book is empty.', replaced by the Book with numbered empty slots that already show what's out there.
references: Google Maps (brand colors checked at https://www.brandcolorcode.com/google-maps: #EA4335, #4285F4, #FBBC04, #1A73E8, #34A853). It's the benchmark for 'where'. psst. wins the first 5 seconds by answering what, when and how before you search (see the concept), and it hands off to Google Maps or Apple Maps from the back of every stub instead of competing on navigation.

Partiful, https://partiful.com (fetched; homepage colors scraped: oranges #F19A38 and #FE8207, pinks, black UI). The bar for playful consumer energy: themes, effects, posters people want to send. psst. takes the 'the object is the share' idea, but every stub is generated from real data (hour, weather, serial) rather than a user-picked theme, and it avoids Partiful's purple-to-pink gradient language (described in a refero.design style excerpt from search).

Things 3, https://culturedcode.com/things/ (fetched): calm daily planning; a reviewer quoted there says 'Each animation is purposeful. Mainly, it is fun.' psst.'s pad is Things' Today for a city: one ordered list, nothing else on screen. It goes further by making the day itself visible as the sky color.

Beli, https://beliapp.com (fetched: 'Track · Share · Discover'). The ranking-by-comparison, city leaderboards and streaks come from search excerpts (today.com, ixd.prattsi.org, Wikipedia), not opened in full. psst. borrows the 'been' habit loop through the Book's numbered slots and neighborhood completion, and drops the leaderboard. Completing Miami is the reward, not out-ranking strangers.

Places by Raya, https://places.app (theme colors checked in page source: #faf7f0 light, #16181a dark), plus App Store listing excerpts from search (curators, a paid 12-month membership; listing not opened). It shows the taste bar: warm off-white, restraint. psst. wins on timing (the right hour and weather on every stub) and on access (free, Miami-specific, and the non-obvious with exact instructions).

Apple Wallet iOS 18 poster event tickets, https://www.passcreator.com/en/solutions/enhanced-event-tickets-in-apple-wallet (fetched): full-bleed artwork, an event guide with weather and a venue map. This is the closest precedent for a ticket that's also a guide. psst. issues tickets for things that have no ticket (a ventanita at 3:05), and the stub becomes a collectible after you go.

Evan Fasquelle portfolio, https://www.evanfasquelle.com/ (fetched; listed on Awwwards under trading-card hover, https://www.awwwards.com/inspiration/hover-effect-evan-fasquelle-portfolio): 'collect all the cards… to unlock new content', 12 cards. The same collect-to-unlock loop as the Book's HOOD DONE, but psst.'s cards are earned by going somewhere real, not by scrolling.

Klangtherapie Festival stackable cards, https://www.awwwards.com/inspiration/stackable-cards-klangtherapie-festival (fetched, by agentur-brandmarker). A stacked-card news pattern with gradients. psst.'s pad uses a stack too, but with paper physics (tear, stamp, punch) and no gradients, so it reads as an object rather than a carousel.

Tilt in use, https://fontsinuse.com/uses/54124/ai-mocap-animation (fetched): Tilt Prism used for a Type@Cooper header because its rotation axes fit a motion-capture course. That's precedent for using Tilt's axes as meaning rather than decoration, which is what the lean-in does.

Checked but not useful or unreachable: godly.website now 301-redirects to recent.design (fetched; the feed had nothing in this category). typewolf.com/recursive returned 404, mobbin.com returned 403 (login wall), and siteinspire's travel filter showed no travel category. The Infatuation, https://www.theinfatuation.com, was checked for color only (#181818 black and #0066F1 blue dominate the source).
antiTemplateChecks: 1. Font check: PASS. Tilt Warp + Recursive, with Tilt Neon limited to the night hour. None are on the template-default list, and each comes from the concept: vinyl-sticker storefront lettering for the collectible ticket; the friend's handwriting (CASL 1) and the ticket printer (MONO 1) in one family.

2. Accent check: PASS with a stated caveat. Mamey #F37F5F is not a library default. Its nearest known color is Partiful's homepage orange #FE8207 (ΔE_OK 0.061, 18° pinker and less saturated), then the Dolphins orange #FC4C02 (0.093). The current #FFC53D fails this check, since it's Bumble's #FFC629.

3. Layout check: PASS. There's no centered hero, feature-card trio, logo row or pricing. The home screen is the signature component itself (a pad of stubs on the sky), and desktop is the map table with the pad as its left column.

4. Device check: PASS. With the wordmark covered, a perforated paper stub with a die-cut sticker and rubber stamp, sitting on a flat sky-colored Biscayne Bay coastline, can't be mistaken for another app.

5. Decoration check: PASS with one deliberate exception. No glass, no backdrop-filter, no decorative gradients. Shadows exist only under paper objects, so they signal elevation. The one glow is the Tilt Neon hour at night, where the glow is the content (lit signage), limited to one element.

6. Voice check: PASS. 'psst. It's 3:05. Here's your move.' / 'Kept. No. 012 is yours. Go before 8.' / 'Closed today and nobody told us. Here's where the regulars went instead.' share a register with the stub copy already in moves.json ('Walk up to the ventanita, order a cafecito…'). The current hero 'SCRUBBING · DAYLIGHT' would fail.

7. Concept check: PASS. (a) Tilt Warp: the move is a collectible you peel and keep, and its letters resemble peeling vinyl stickers. (b) Mamey means now: a ticket is valid for a time, so the accent marks the present moment. (c) The perforation: keeping a friend's tip is a physical gesture, so saving is tearing, not tapping a heart.
risks: Tilt Warp can tip into toy-like if overused. Keep it at 20px and up, ink or paper only, never in paragraphs, never all caps. Fallbacks I tested on the same stub: Anybody 800 (the current face: competent but anonymous) and Shrikhand (strong, but a one-weight retro italic that reads as a diner menu). Collletttivo's Coconat (Sara Lavazza, OFL per https://www.collletttivo.it/typefaces/coconat) is the editorial alternate, but it would need base64 inlining and I haven't measured its size. Other foundries I checked: Velvetyne (https://velvetyne.fr/about/) is OFL for commercial and web use but asks you to credit the designer and the foundry; none of its faces combine storefront-sign roots with rotation axes, so none is used. Collletttivo (Apfel Grotezk, Aujournuit, Coconat pages) is OFL. Use & Modify (https://usemodify.com/) mixes GPL, CC and OFL licenses, so each font would need its own license check before inlining; none is used. The League of Moveable Type (https://www.theleagueofmoveabletype.com/) is OFL; League Gothic was the 'ADMIT ONE' ticket-caps candidate, but Recursive Mono covers the printer role without adding a third family.

Fontshare is excluded on purpose. I couldn't open the ITF Free Font License text (the Fontshare license page is a client-rendered app), and the secondhand quotes forbid 'uploading them in a public server' and modification, which base64-inlining into a published artifact arguably does. Use only OFL faces.

CSP: Google Fonts stylesheets pull font files from fonts.gstatic.com (and text= subsets from fonts.gstatic.com/l/font). Confirm font-src allows them in the artifact sandbox, as the current build implies. Otherwise base64 the OFL files: about 68 KB + 142 KB + 21.5 KB woff2, roughly 310 KB as base64.

A swipeable card stack can read as Tinder. Swipe means 'next hour', never like or dislike, and the paper physics (tear, stamp, punch) has to carry the difference. If the tear interaction feels fiddly in testing, the button alone must still work in one tap plus a confirm.

The daily ritual needs content. With 43 moves and 8 sealed secrets (secret=2), the 3:05 drop repeats after 8 days and Today pads repeat within a week. The ritual needs roughly 150 moves and a weekly secret budget, plus the 45 events rotated into pads, before locals will open it weekly.

Sky-field contrast is safe for text (ink on every light sky is 8.1:1 or better, paper on dusk and night 6.2:1 or better), but sticker inks can vanish on matching skies: pool on morning, ventanita on noon, mamey on golden. Every emblem keeps its 3px paper die-cut border, and every sticker ink needs testing against all seven skies before ship.
Golden hour turning the whole screen warm breaks the 'one accent per view' rule. It's deliberate, and it has to stay limited to sunset-60 to sunset+15, or the owned color stops meaning 'now'.

Honesty rules: serials (No. 012/043) must be stable real indices, travel minutes need geolocation or a labeled origin ('from Brickell'), weather on Nov 20–24 must say 'typical', and nothing on a share card may imply live data it doesn't have.

Performance on mid-range phones: the canvas map, traffic particles and per-frame sky changes. Cap DPR at 2, rebuild the map cache only on a meaningful color change, pause rAF when document.hidden, and never use backdrop-filter.

judges.lens: Awwwards/FWA juror scoring Design, Creativity, Innovation and Content against the brief's own bar (playful, colorful, phone-first on the street, everything real or labeled, metaphors die if they read as costume). For each direction I ask which single phone screenshot gets sent to a friend, and which award-site lineage it borrows from.

strengths: The screenshot people send: the chrome-yellow HOY board at golden hour, its painted letters casting a long drop shade to the right because the sun really is in the west, then the same board after sunset. It is the only direction whose signature passes the logo-covered test on a single phone screenshot.

The sun shade is new to this category and it carries information: it comes from NOAA solar position at the dial hour, so 'type that knows where the sun is' meets the real-or-labeled rule. No award site I can name does this.
Interactions are verbs tied to real actions: tear a tab to add to the plan, peel tape to reveal a secret, print to share. Juries reward that over decorative motion.

The deepest Miami content: ventanita boards, wheat-paste poles, William Lane tower colors, Little Haiti sign painting. The tightest voice too: 'HOY, 4:42PM. Two good moves before the sun goes at 7:06.'

The most accurate critique of r0. It traces the THUNDE/RCAT break to overflow-wrap:anywhere, measures #FFC53D within 2 degrees of Bumble's hue, and catches the slot bug, the two clocks, and blurred secrets reading as a rendering bug.
It keeps and re-skins the real OSM map, the dial, the lean-in hold, the receipt and the flyers. The desktop map never disappears.
weaknesses: About 13 metaphors at once: board, flyer, receipt, ticket stub, sticker, domino, price gun, masking tape, rubber stamps, binder clip, index-divider tabs, accordion map, crop marks. The hotel metaphor was killed for less. As specced it is a scrapbook theme park.

Lineage: paper, riso, grain, torn edges and tape are the 2020-25 Awwwards zine trope. The receipt is Receiptify (2020), and stickers-as-personality is Partiful and Gopher. Only the sun shade and the sunset flip are new.

The night palette contradicts its own 'NOT Miami Vice neon' line. uv/pink #FF3EA5, uv/cyan #3DF2E0 and uv/lime on near-black is the Vice palette, and it would ship the week GTA VI launches (Nov 19, the day before the test trip).
Four type families. Tilt Warp is wide and single-weight. 'HOY' breaks its own rule of Spanish only for real nouns (it's an adverb), so test it with Miami locals before it reads as costume.
On mobile the map, the codebase's only bespoke asset, shrinks to a 152px folded strip, and effort goes into an accordion-unfold gimmick.
The performance stack is risky on mid-range Android: up to 15 stacked text-shadows on three headlines, YROT re-rasterizing, canvas traffic and grain together.
The domino glyph is clever but needs a legend. First-use comprehension is unproven.

scores.direction: Tear Here: today's Miami as a pad of tear-off moves
strengths: The best product. It is the only direction that puts one complete move (what, when, why, how) in the first viewport before any animation, so it wins Usability outright.
The screenshot people send: the whole screen turned mamey/golden at sunset minus 60 minutes, with a paper stub on it reading 'good till 8pm'.

The only direction with a reason for locals to open it weekly: the 3:05 daily drop (cafecito plus the 305 area code), the Thursday 'This weekend' pad, and the Book by neighborhood with numbered empty slots and HOOD DONE.
One object system (the stub), so it has the lowest metaphor count and the most coherence of the three.

The planner is specced as hard, unit-tested rules: a move sits inside its open windows and within ±90 min of its best time, the slot label derives from the time, no day is empty, and both John Summit nights are anchors.

The best lines: 'psst. It's 3:05. Here's your move.' and 'Closed today and nobody told us. Here's where the regulars went instead.' It also solves Tilt Warp's proportional digits with fixed cells so the scrubbed hour doesn't jitter.
weaknesses: Lineage: a swipe card stack is Tinder (a real jury deduction), the ticket is Apple Wallet poster tickets and DICE, a flat time-of-day sky is Apple Weather and Weather Line, and the collection book is Beli. A jury has seen every piece of it.
It demotes the map, the only bespoke asset, to tone-on-tone wallpaper on mobile, so 'where' is lost at a glance.

Self-contradictions: it keeps the abstract Sticker.svelte gradient art as the emblem (non-collectible), brings blur back into the lean-in after cutting blurred text, and breaks its own one-accent rule at golden hour.
The pastel sky stops (pool blue, seafoam, cream at noon) read as a calm lifestyle app, not jaw-dropping. That is below the founder's 'colorful, playful' bar.

A 470px stub shows one move per screen, so comparing seven options takes seven swipes. Holding 650ms to tear is fiddly on the street, and a DeviceOrientation permission prompt for a tilting headline is a gimmick.
By its own count the ritual needs about 150 moves to avoid repeats, so with 43 moves it can't be built yet.

strengths: The screenshot people send: Lights On. The coastline draws itself as a line of light from Key Biscayne northward, then the roads switch on, then one amber beacon pillar lands on the move. The Long Exposure stay poster is a second one.
The best idea about the map: only what is actually open at the dial hour glows (glow() already exists). The light is the data, which is beauty and honesty at once.
The most concrete day-mode fix: a distance-from-coast water ramp (shallows to channel), greedy label collision boxes, and a beacon shadow cast from the sun's azimuth.
The strictest accent rule (one beacon per view) and the best performance engineering: sprite-and-streak traffic, bloom at 1/8 size, a frame budget that auto-degrades.
Data-driven variable type axes (energy sets weight, secrecy sets width, late night sets slant) are real typographic innovation.
The mobile first-paint budget is worked out to the pixel.
weaknesses: Lineage: the most derivative genre of the three. City lights at night is Mapbox night presets, Uber, every WebGL 'data city', and La Phase 5's Marseille SOTD. Cover the logo and it is a map wallpaper.
It fails the brief's 'colorful, playful': moody, cinematic, letterboxed. The least fun direction.
It names the GTA VI risk, then designs straight into it: a Bank Gothic revival over neon Miami at night, in launch week.
The 'window seat' concept barely reaches the UI. It is a camera tilt and a name, a metaphor with no object behind it.
Science Gothic as 16px body text is mechanical, and the display face weighs 156 KB.
Illustrative boats, wakes, traffic and pools are invented content in a product whose rule is real-or-labeled. A truth line in the corner admits the problem rather than fixing it.

Its critique has a factual error. It blames shots.mjs for reusing one page with hash navigation, but shots.mjs opens a fresh page per view (browser.newPage() inside the loop). The blank desktop map on Plan, Wall, You, Move and Event is still unexplained.
Title cards replace stickers, so nothing tactile is left to collect or send.

judges.winner: Painted Fresh (Street Print), on one condition: cut it to five objects (HOY board, flyer wall, receipt, sticker, tape) plus the sun shade, and replace the night UV trio. The tie-breaker against Tear Here was the logo-covered phone screenshot. Sign lettering whose drop shade follows Miami's real sun is ownable. A flat sky-colored screen with a ticket stub is what weather apps and Apple Wallet already look like. Tear Here is the better product skeleton, so its product rules get grafted in wholesale.
grafts: From Tear Here: a first-viewport rule. At 390x844, one complete move (name, time window, one-line why, Go) must be visible above the tabs before any animation runs. The HOY board's #1 strip expands to carry 'the move' line.

From Tear Here: planner hard rules, unit-tested. A move only sits inside its open windows on that weekday, within ±90 min of its best time; the slot label derives from the time (never the reverse); 2-4 stops a day with no empty days; John Summit nights 1 and 2 are fixed anchors; landing and flight-out times clip the first and last days.

From Tear Here: the 3:05 drop. At 15:05 Miami time a taped secret strip slides onto the HOY board, chosen by day-of-year. On Thursdays at 15:05 the board header becomes 'THIS WEEKEND'. Don't ship it until there are enough secrets that it doesn't repeat inside two weeks.

From Tear Here: Pocket becomes the Book. One page per neighborhood with numbered die-cut outlines and a one-line clue each, and a HOOD DONE stamp that unlocks that hood's secret. This replaces 'Your sticker book is empty.'

From Tear Here: a golden-hour takeover. From sunset minus 60 to sunset plus 15 the table color itself warms to full golden. It is the one sanctioned break of the one-accent rule and the screenshot moment, and it's honest because it's the real sky.
From Tear Here: fixed-width digit cells for Tilt Warp's proportional numerals, so the live clock and the scrubbed hour never jitter.
From Tear Here: 'Show me where'. The strip's sticker FLIPs onto the venue on the map with squash-and-stretch, plus a dotted walking line labeled 'from Brickell' when location is off.
From Tear Here: test Recursive (MONO 1 for the receipt and data, sans for body) as a replacement for Martian Mono plus Atkinson, which would cut the system from four families to three.
From Night Flight: glow only what is open at the dial hour (existing glow()). This replaces r0's generic cyan coastline glow and pink radial blobs.

From Night Flight: Lights On as the sunset event. The coastline draws from Key Biscayne north and roads switch on by distance from the coast over 1.2s, fused with Painted Fresh's paper-to-night flip so day-to-night is one moment.

From Night Flight: day water as a distance-from-coast ramp (shallows #82E1E0 to channel #117FAA, re-tuned to the paper palette), plus greedy label collision boxes so 'ALLAPATTAHDESIGN DISTRICT' and clipped 'MID-BEA' can't recur.
From Night Flight: a traffic renderer with two pre-rendered sprites plus streaks, a 600/280 particle budget, auto-halving after 3 slow frames, and rAF paused on document.hidden.
From Night Flight: a sun rail painted with the light model's actual colors for today's date, plus the honest scrub line 'AT 9:30PM · NOW 4:42PM'.
From Night Flight: data-driven type axes on strip names. League Gothic wdth narrows with secret level and tracks energy, so each name encodes its move.
From Night Flight: harness discipline. Every review gets a 10s motion capture of the sun scrub and the sunset flip, because reduced-motion stills can't show this direction's signature.
mustNotShip: Painted Fresh's night palette as specced: uv/pink, uv/cyan and uv/lime on coal. That is the Miami Vice / Vice City palette, shipping the week GTA VI launches. Night should be warm sodium and headlight light with piña as the one fluorescent ink.

All 13 paper metaphors at once. Cut the binder clip, crop-mark focus states, the accordion folded map, four-stock index-divider tabs, fire-outlined rubber-stamp filters, and price-gun labels on more than one item per view.
Grain, riso misregistration and torn edges as global texture. A grain overlay on everything is the most overused award-site cliché of 2022-25.

Generic award-site moves: a percentage preloader, a custom cursor, smooth-scroll hijacking, marquee tickers, text-scramble effects, and any blocking intro (r0's 1.9s splash or a paint-on that delays the answer).
Blurred text as a 'secret', in any form: r0's blurred names or Tear Here's blur-to-sharp lean-in.
Night Flight's Science Gothic/Bank Gothic over a neon night (GTA fan art), its 38-degree cinematic tilt and letterbox bands, and illustrative boats, wakes and pools on a real-or-labeled product.

Tear Here's swipe-left/right card stack as the main way to browse moves, a DeviceOrientation permission prompt for a tilting headline, the neon-flicker hour, and keeping the abstract gradient Sticker.svelte art.
Sound or haptics on by default, including a synthesized 'psst' whisper or printer buzz. Opt-in only, and never in v1 if time is short.
Any number that looks live but isn't: travel minutes without a labeled origin, Nov 20-24 weather without FCST/TYP, traffic without 'illustrative', dollar prices beyond the m.cost tier.
Spanish or Kreyòl used as decoration ('HOY' included) until Miami locals have seen it. No Spanglish jokes, no fake handwriting, no imitation of a named living sign painter.
buildOrder: 1. Truth fixes before any new skin. Planner hard rules with unit tests (open windows, ±90 min of best, label from time, no empty days, both John Summit nights, FCST vs TYP on every day). Flyer fit-text: League Gothic wdth 100 down to 75, size 64 down to 22, break only at spaces, date printed once. One live clock: a scrub reads 'AT 9:30PM' and never replaces the live time. Delete blurred secrets. Reproduce and fix the blank desktop map on Plan, Wall, You, Move and Event in a real browser; it is not a hash-nav artifact, because shots.mjs opens a fresh page per view.

2. Layout skeleton. On desktop the map is the permanent tabletop with the active object in cols 1-4. On mobile the first viewport is header, map strip, and the HOY board with the #1 move complete above the 64px tabs. Delete glass/backdrop-filter, 28px cards, all pills, the stock icon tab bar and the wrapping six-filter row (use one non-wrapping row of five toggles).

3. Tokens. Piña #FFB01F, one object per view. Thermal and newsprint papers by day, coffee-tinted coal at night. No purple-navy and no Vice UV trio. Type is Tilt Warp (28px and up, 1-4 words), League Gothic for names, Martian Mono for data; test Recursive as the body/data family to cut to three.

4. The signature first, then judge it on a phone. Add solarPosition() to core.js. Put the sun shade on at most 3 headlines per view with the YROT peel, driven by the dial and Play the day. Reduced motion keeps the values and drops the transitions. If it doesn't read as 'the sun' on an iPhone outdoors, stop and rethink before building anything else.

5. Map re-light. Day: distance-field water ramp plus label collision. All hours: only what's open at the dial hour glows. Sunset: one event, the Lights On wave plus the table flipping to night papers. Traffic: the sprite renderer with its frame budget.

6. HOY board. Letter-board strips (name, dotted leader, best time, domino, status). A piña tip label on #1 only. The taped secret with the 950ms peel, also on Enter/Space. The golden-hour table takeover. Flip-in letter changes capped at 24 characters per strip.

7. Wheat-paste Wall. Kraft ground, a split-fountain ink keyed to start time, and the tear-off fringe as one accessible button that arcs into PLAN and bumps its count. Dates outside the stay land in Pocket as 'HELD' with 'Extend stay'.

8. Receipt and Book. A thermal receipt with an order-slip skin over the native inputs, a dot-matrix energy chart, an 18ms-per-line print, and a navigator.share PNG. Pocket becomes the neighborhood Book, with text-led die-cut stickers slapped onto the map on 'I went', then the 3:05 drop once content allows. Cut first if time runs out: the scannable Code 128, the paint-on intro, the accordion unfold, sound.

judges.lens: I judged this as the founder (MBA student, former elite athlete, startup CEO who wants to be wowed and can spot generic AI output) and his friend visiting Miami Nov 20-24 for John Summit at Kaseya Center. The questions: would we open this instead of Google Maps and Instagram, is it fun, is it beautiful, would people talk about it as a brand. I ran the brand checks from the directing-brand-design skill: one idea held hard, one or two graphic devices, one owned accent used once per view, and no template defaults. Evidence: BRIEF.md, the r0 shots and the newer r1-data shots, Flyer.svelte, the planner in core.js lines 180-240, and moves.json (43 moves). Three caveats. (1) r1-data/desktop-wall.png shows the map rendering on Wall, so the empty navy right side in the r0 desktop shots is almost certainly a capture bug in shots.mjs (it navigates by URL hash on one page), not a design flaw. Stop judging it. (2) The GTA VI release date of Nov 19, 2026 comes from Night Flight's own research. My search to re-check it was rate-limited. (3) The three 'critique of current' sections say nearly the same thing (ALLAPATTAH label collision, THUNDE/RCAT word break, cafecito slotted at sunset, Bumble yellow), so they didn't separate the directions. I scored on concept count, first-screen answer, owned accent, share artifact, fun and build risk.

scores.direction: Tear Here: today's Miami as a pad of tear-off moves
strengths: It's the only direction designed around the job. About 0.6s after opening, the top stub says what to do, when, how far away it is, and what to order. That beats Google Maps on 'what' and Instagram on 'when', and it's the first thing the friend would actually act on.
It's one object (the stub) on one background (the sky). It passes the 'one idea held hard' test the hotel metaphor failed, and the founder can pitch it in one sentence.
Mamey #F37F5F is the only proposed accent that leaves the yellow family. 'Mamey means now' is a usage rule with meaning. 'The coral one' is something people can say; 'the other yellow one' isn't.
The sky field is honest about time and looks good in a screenshot. The whole screen is the color of Miami's sky this minute, and golden hour turns the phone orange. That's the screenshot people send.
It's the only direction with a reason for locals to come back weekly (daily pad, 3:05 secret drop, Thursday weekend pad) plus a visitor view, the Strip. That's the retention story an MBA can defend.

Planner rules are written as unit-tested hard constraints: only inside opening windows, within 90 minutes of the best time, labels derived from the time, no empty days, both John Summit nights included.
It's the leanest system: two families (Tilt Warp and Recursive) plus a 21KB Tilt Neon digits subset, and the lowest build risk on a mid-range phone.
weaknesses: The one-card-at-a-time swipe stack reads as Tinder. A visitor deciding tonight wants to see two or three options at once, not swipe blind.
On mobile the map becomes a label-free backdrop in the sky color. Miami's geography effectively disappears until you tap 'Show me where'.
At noon the flat pastel skies (pool blue, seafoam, sun-bleached) can read as a wellness or meditation app. Only golden hour and night carry the drama.
It breaks its own no-pun voice: the 'cafecito o'clock' lede and the pineapple-to-cup morph are a pun and a doodle.
The Apple Maps / Google Maps hand-off is on the back of the stub, so you have to flip it first. The friend on the street needs Go on the front.
43 moves and 8 secrets can't sustain a daily ritual: the 3:05 drop repeats after 8 days.
It kills the Receipt, the most shareable thing the current app has.
Stubs, perforations, stamps and stickers are still the ephemera vocabulary that AI-generated 'playful' UI leans on. It only stays clean if each view keeps to one or two of them.

strengths: It's the most Miami-specific and best-researched world: the ventanita board, the 3:05 cafecito, Little Haiti sign painting, William Lane's lifeguard-tower colors. It's the only one a local would recognize as Miami rather than 'a city'.
The sun-driven drop shade is the best single device across all three directions. The shadow under the lettering comes from real sun-position math, so it carries information instead of decorating.
The blacklight flip at sunset gives night real color without falling into the Miami Vice / GTA neon cliché. It's the most colorful and playful direction against the brief.
The flyer tear-off tab is the best Wall interaction proposed. Tearing a tab adds the event to the plan, and an event outside the stay goes to Pocket marked 'HELD' with an 'EXTEND STAY' option.
The thermal receipt is a proven share format, and 'NO REFUNDS ON SUNSETS' is a line people would quote.
It did the most rigorous contrast and font-license homework of the three.
weaknesses: It repeats the rejected hotel metaphor's failure at roughly 12 times the density: ventanita board, wheat-paste wall, receipt, ticket stub, sticker, price gun, rubber stamps, masking tape, domino, binder clip, index tabs, barcode, crop marks, perforations, accordion folds. That fails the skill's 'one or two devices' rule and is the clearest AI-output sign on the table.
Four type families (Tilt Warp, League Gothic, Martian Mono, Atkinson) reads like a type specimen, not a brand.
In a still screenshot the sun shade looks like retro drop-shadow type (Canva, diner retro). The concept only shows while you're dragging the time.
Piña #FFB01F (hue 75.1) is the same color as Night Flight's Beacon #FFB127 (hue 75.0). Both moved about 11° off Bumble's yellow, and neither owns the color.

First screen: header, folded map, HOY header, hero line, sun rail and five stamps all come before the moves. That leaves about 2.5 move names above the tab bar and no instruction for what to do there.
The domino glyph for energy and cost needs a legend, and the direction admits the comprehension risk itself.
It has the highest build cost, much of it theater: an opentype paint-on intro, a Code 128 barcode, a WebAudio printer buzz, an accordion map unfold and per-letter flips.
It gives locals no reason to come back weekly.

strengths: 'Only what's open glows', computed from real opening hours and the real sun, is the most honest data-driven visual idea on the table.
The Beacon card comes with an explicit first-screen budget at 390x844: one complete answer plus one alternative above the fold. Its Go button is a plain Maps link.
It's the most realistic engineering plan: sprite-based traffic, a 6ms frame budget, automatic downgrade when frames run slow, and a truth line that labels traffic and boats as illustrative.
It's the only direction that correctly diagnosed the desktop void as a shots.mjs capture bug and noticed the shots were taken with reduced motion. r1-data confirms the first point.
The desktop letterbox frame is the most Awwwards-ready single image.
weaknesses: It's r0 done well. The brief names 'dark map template' as the weakness, and r1-data's night map with traffic dots and pink glows already exists and was still 'not good enough'.
Neon night-time Miami plus a Bank Gothic revival during the week GTA VI launches (Nov 19 per its own research, the day before the test trip) will read as fan art.
It's the least playful and least colorful by day. Scrubbing is the only thing to touch, and Science Gothic is cold and mechanical for a brand that's supposed to be a friend.
It fights Google Maps on Google's turf, a map, instead of winning on what to do and when.
Encoding secrecy and energy in title-card font axes is legible only to the designer.
It's the heaviest canvas workload for a phone used on the street: distance-field water, bloom, reflections and boats.
The Beacon accent is the same yellow as Painted Fresh's piña.
By its own admission, the day mode has to carry the brand's ownership, and it hasn't been tested.

judges.winner: Tear Here wins because it's the only direction where the first screen is the answer. The friend lands at 3pm on Nov 20, opens psst. and sees one move with the time, the walk and what to order, before Google Maps has even loaded its search bar. It's also the only one with one idea, one owned non-yellow accent, and a weekly reason for locals to return. Painted Fresh should be the source of grafts, not the runner-up system: its sun shade, blacklight night, flyer tear-off and receipt voice are the best individual ideas, and its whole kit is the slop risk. Night Flight gives the map honesty rule and the performance discipline.
grafts: From Painted Fresh: the sun-driven drop shade, used in ONE place only, on Tilt Warp's big hour numerals. The offset comes from real solar azimuth and altitude for Miami (25.7617, -80.1918), so the shadow swings as you drag the time. It's information, not decoration, and the only shaded type in the system.

From Painted Fresh: the blacklight night. After sunset the sky goes near-black, and the night map and 'open now' dots switch to UV lime and pink. Stubs stay paper. This gives night real color instead of Tear Here's flat navy, and avoids GTA neon.

From Painted Fresh: fitted flyer titles. Step the type size down from 64 to 22px until every word fits, break lines only at spaces, and let footers wrap to two lines instead of truncating ('THE GROUND (CLU…' still truncates in r1-data). Add split-fountain inks keyed to start time (before 6pm, 6pm to midnight, after midnight) so the Wall is color-coded by when things happen.
From Painted Fresh: the flyer tear-off tab adds the event straight to the Trip, with the stay-date logic. An event outside Nov 20-24 goes to the Book marked 'HELD', with an 'Extend stay' option.

From Painted Fresh: receipt voice and honesty labels. Every temperature reads FCST or TYP, and the Strip's text export keeps the thermal-receipt format with tail lines like 'NO REFUNDS ON SUNSETS'. That's the group-chat version; the 1080x1920 PNG is the Stories version.

From Night Flight: only what's open glows. On the sky-colored map, every venue open at the scrubbed hour shows as a small ink dot, and the top stub's venue is the single mamey point. Add the corner truth line 'LIGHT FROM REAL OPENING HOURS'. This gives the mobile backdrop real information instead of pure mood.
From Night Flight: one clock. While scrubbing, the credit line reads 'AT 9:30PM · NOW 4:42PM', so a scrubbed time never looks like the present.

From Night Flight: Lights On at sunset. When the time crosses sunset, roads and open spots switch on in a wave from the coast inland over 1.2s, paired with the hour switching to Tilt Neon. Drop Tear Here's flicker.

From Night Flight: the Beacon card's first-screen rules. Put a 48px 'Go' (Apple Maps on iOS, Google Maps elsewhere) on the FRONT of the top stub, and budget the 390x844 layout so the stub's title, note and both actions sit above the tab bar.

From Night Flight: the traffic renderer and performance budget (two pre-rendered sprites, 280 particles on mobile, halve particles and drop bloom after 3 frames over 20ms), and light-trail routes between Trip stops on the desktop map.

From Night Flight: fix the screenshot script and capture motion. Reshoot on real moves.json with full motion, and add a 10-second recording of the sky scrub and the tear, so the next review judges the real product.
mustNotShip: Blurred text as a 'secret', and a locked secret inside a visitor's Trip. r1-data's 1am 'A secret spot (lean in to see)' gives the friend nothing he can act on.
Any yellow accent within about 15° of Bumble's hue: r0's #FFC53D, Painted Fresh's #FFB01F and Night Flight's #FFB127 all fail ownership.

Painted Fresh's full kit together: masking tape, binder clip, price-gun labels, crop marks, accordion creases, paper grain, riso misregistration, rubber stamps, index tabs. More than two of these per view is scrapbook slop.
Four type families. Hold to Tilt Warp plus Recursive, with Tilt Neon only for the night hour.
Letter-board character flips on every re-ranking. While scrubbing, that's motion noise.
The domino glyph for energy and cost. Write 'low-key · $$' instead.
The Code 128 barcode and the WebAudio thermal-printer buzz. Theater: nobody scans a code that's printed right above it.
The first-visit paint-on wordmark, which needs an opentype.js build step.
Night as the default identity, and neon Miami with Bank Gothic type in GTA VI launch week.
Night Flight's 38° cinematic camera tilt that disables taps.
Font axes that encode data (narrow means secret, slanted means late). Nobody but the designer can read it.
A synthesized 'psst' whisper. Filtered white noise will sound like static.
Science Gothic as body text.
Swipe-left/right card semantics. Show a visible stack with a 'Next' control and a three-stub overview of later today.
A DeviceOrientation permission prompt just to tilt the hour.
The 'cafecito o'clock' pun and the pineapple-to-coffee-cup morph.
Hole-punch 'WENT' stamps and a 'HOOD DONE' unlock economy that reads as Pokémon Go. Keep a quiet count.
A daily 3:05 secret drop while there are only 8 secrets. Make it weekly until the pool supports daily.
Letting the golden-hour all-orange screen run outside the window from 60 minutes before sunset to 15 minutes after, which would kill 'mamey means now'.
Pink-orange-purple sunset gradients, flamingos, Miami Vice neon, Spanglish jokes, airport puns.
Developer jargon in the UI ('SCRUBBING · DAYLIGHT'), and two clocks that disagree.
Filler copy like 'COST less than you think', and any day in the plan that prints empty.
Fontshare / ITF fonts inside the artifact. Their license bars subsetting and requires embedded fonts to be non-extractable.
Glass panels, backdrop blur, pill chips, the six-chip filter row, and the stock four-icon tab bar.
buildOrder: 1. Truth pass before any pixels: unit-test the planner against real moves.json. A move can only be placed inside its weekday opening windows and within 90 minutes of its best time. Labels come from both the time and the move's category: r1-data still calls a frozen martini 'DINNER' and routes Key Biscayne, then Little River, then Kaseya in Friday rush hour. Every day gets 2-4 stops, John Summit night 2 is included, there are no locked secrets in visitor plans, and every temperature says FCST or TYP. core.js already checks openAt and bestFit, so the r0 sunrise-swim-at-dinner may have been placeholder data; fix both the data and the logic. In the same pass: one live clock, fitted flyer titles with no mid-word breaks, and fix shots.mjs and reshoot with motion on.

2. Mobile Today first screen: sky-field background, the 76px hour, the time track, a one-line lede, and the top stub with title, note, 'Go' and 'Keep', all above the tab bar at 390x844. Delete the bottom sheet, glass, the MIA chip, the recenter button, the six filter pills and the Dial UI.

3. System swap in one pass: Tilt Warp plus Recursive (Tilt Neon digits subset at night), mamey as the single 'now' accent once per view, ink pills, and a text-only paper tab bar. Remove #FFC53D, Anybody, Figtree, DM Mono and the purple navy.

4. The stub component and the tear, the signature interaction: hold or drag to tear along the perforation, a KEPT stamp, and the stub flies to the Book. Keep a one-tap button path, and do a 120ms crossfade under reduced motion.

5. Sky scrub that carries information: interpolate the 7 sky stops in OKLab, draw the map in the sky color with open-now dots and the single mamey beacon, add the sun-shade on the hour only, and at sunset switch the hour to Tilt Neon with the Lights On wave and blacklight night inks.

6. Trip Strip for Nov 20-24, the friend's reason to switch from Instagram: John Summit nights as event stubs, a 1080x1920 PNG shared via navigator.share (download fallback after awaiting document.fonts.ready), and the receipt-format text for the group chat. Confirm the share path works inside the sandboxed artifact before promising a Save button.
7. Wall: fitted flyer titles, time-keyed split-fountain inks, tear-off tabs that add to the Trip with the outside-the-stay handling, and day stubs instead of pills.

8. Desktop table: the pad as a left column over an always-on live map with venue stickers, hover linking between stub and sticker, light-trail routes on Trip, and the Later strip along the bottom. Then the Book (one page per neighborhood) and a weekly 3:05 drop, sized to the real secret pool.

judges.lens: Senior design engineer. The question is what I can build to full polish in about a day as a Svelte 5 single-file artifact, at 60fps on a mid-range phone, accessible, and inside the artifact's CSP and sandbox. I score on polish surface, meaning how many separate things must all be finished before the concept lands, not on taste. Evidence gathered this session: I read BRIEF.md, 8 of the 18 r0 shots, and MiamiMap.svelte, Flyer.svelte, App.svelte, index.html and shots.mjs. I benchmarked in headless Chrome at 390x844, DPR 3, with 4x and 6x CPU throttle. Result 1: a 15-layer text-shadow on three 88px Tilt Warp headlines, updated every frame, costs about 0.7-1.1ms p50 of main-thread work. Animating YROT on top of that raises it to about 1.5ms p50 and 4.3ms p95. Paint and raster were not measured. Result 2: on canvas, a radial gradient per car costs about 3x a pre-rendered sprite. That is a relative number only, because the absolute ms are skewed by per-frame readback and DPR 3. Result 3: in Chrome, ctx.fontStretch does reach Science Gothic's wdth axis ('MIAMI' measured 208px, then 325px at ultra-expanded). Canvas has no API for YROT, XROT, CASL, MONO or CTRS, so no share image can use those axes. Safari was not tested. Result 4: geo.json holds only land, coast and roads, with 0 pool features. Result 5: moves.json has 43 moves, 8 of them secret=2. Result 6: the artifact-capabilities contract says file saves go through claude.use('downloads').save() with a viewer confirmation, and png is on the allowlist. r0 already has a 'Copy blocked here' clipboard fallback, so sandbox API failures are real. Result 7: App.svelte line 49 renders MiamiMap on every tab, so the empty navy void on the desktop shots is a draw or capture bug, not a layout decision. shots.mjs now opens a new page per view, so Night Flight's 'reused page' explanation doesn't match the current script either. Not verified: the GTA VI release date (web search was rate-limited).

scores.direction: Tear Here: today's Miami as a pad of tear-off moves
strengths: Smallest polish surface of the three. There is one object, the stub, with five states, on a flat CSS color field. Events reuse the same object, so one well-finished component carries Today, Trip and Book. That is the only plan that can look finished in a day.

The sky field is the cheapest high-impact change available: an OKLab lerp between seven stops written to one CSS variable. It needs no canvas and no per-frame raster, and it fixes r0's bland mint day mode immediately (pool blue, seafoam, golden #FCA864, sea grape). Stubs stay paper in every state, so text contrast never depends on the hour (ink on every light sky is 8.1:1 or better).
Tone-on-tone map with no labels by day is cheaper than r0's map, and it removes the label collisions ('ALLAPATTAHDESIGN DISTRICT') by not drawing labels at all.

Two families plus a 21.5KB Tilt Neon digit subset. Recursive with wght/CASL/MONO only (142KB) gives a note voice, a UI voice and a printer voice from one file. Fixed 0.62em digit cells stop the hour from jittering while scrubbing. That is a real engineering detail someone thought about.

The tear interaction can be built well: a clip-path polygon along a jagged path seeded by mulberry32, plus a FLIP into the tab using getBoundingClientRect. The specified hold, drag, Enter and reduced-motion crossfade cover input and accessibility.
The planner gets hard rules as unit tests (inside open windows, within ±90 min of best, slot label derived from the time, no empty days). That makes the data trustworthy before anything is drawn.
It answers what, when and how on the first screen. One stub at a time is the strongest answer to 'not one move visible above the tab bar'.
weaknesses: The stub is too tall. A 470px stub plus the 76px hour, track, lede, wordmark and 64px tabs sums to about 818px on a chrome-less 844 frame. In Safari with its bars (about 664px usable), inside the artifact frame, 'Hold to tear' falls below the fold. The 'clamp the note to 3 lines' fix doesn't close a 150-200px gap.

It keeps r0's Sticker.svelte art, the abstract gradient app-icon blobs that both other directions correctly call generic, as the emblem on every stub and pin. This is the one place the direction is still r0.
The swipe stack is the fiddliest component on the list (velocity, thresholds, rotation, focus management) and reads as Tinder. If it ships half-tuned, the whole product feels like a demo.

'Show me where' (the stub morphs into a 36px sticker while the canvas view tweens to 4x) is L effort with two animation systems that must stay in sync. It is the likeliest jank point on a mid-range phone.

The lean-in tilt uses DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission inside a sandboxed cross-origin iframe, and it brings back letter-by-letter un-blur, the blurred-secret pattern its own cut list removes.

Its share card uses canvas.toBlob, then navigator.share or a[download]. Neither is the artifact save path. The direction also admits canvas can't draw CASL/MONO, so the share card won't match the stub.
On desktop, a label-free tone-on-tone map across about 970px risks reading as an empty pastel wash unless the pad's stickers and the Later strip actually populate it.
Tilt Neon's text= subset is served from a separate gstatic path that nobody has confirmed loads inside the published artifact.

strengths: The sun shade is the best owned device in all three proposals, and it's cheap. A text-shadow stack driven by the real solar azimuth costs about 1ms p50 of main-thread work for three 88px headlines at 4-6x throttle, and adding YROT animation brings it to about 1.5ms p50 (paint not measured). Cover the logo and it still reads as psst.

It has the most rigorous accessibility and contrast spec. Every text pair is computed, banned pairs are named (fire on piña 2.76:1), there are visible crop-mark focus states, keyboard equivalents for hold and drag, and the live clock is never replaced by a scrubbed time.
The flyer fit-text algorithm is correct and small: League Gothic wdth 100 down to 75, then size 64 down to 22, measured with measureText, breaking only at spaces. It directly kills 'THUNDE / RCAT'.

The tear-off fringe on the Wall adds the event to the plan. The edge case where the event falls outside the stay (it goes to Pocket marked 'Held', with an 'Extend stay' option and a polite status line) is real product engineering, not decoration.
The receipt is upgraded with honest FCST/TYP labels, a real Code 128 barcode (about 60 lines of JS) and a steps() line feed. All of that can be built well in a few hours.
The one-piña-object-per-view rule is written into the tokens, so the accent can't spread the way r0's #FFC53D did.
weaknesses: Largest polish surface by far, about 3 weeks of work billed as a day. Every one of these has to look finished: HOY board, sun rail, rubber stamps, letter-board strips, masking tape, price-gun label, domino, wheat-paste wall, tear-off fringe, receipt, ticket stub, die-cut stickers, binder clip, index-divider tabs, folded map, Pocket map. On top of that come 4 type families, 4 light states, 4 synthesized sounds and 8 'jaw-drop' moments. One day gets maybe 30% of it, and the other 70% ships looking half-done.
It is a kitchen sink of print metaphors with no single hero object. Board, flyer, receipt, ticket, sticker, tape, stamp and price gun all compete for attention.

The parts most likely to look cheap are the masking-tape curl (in CSS it becomes a grey rectangle), the paint-on intro tracing opentype outlines (reads as an SVG tutorial, not a brush), the full-screen kraft wall with feTurbulence grain (muddy brown, which works against 'colorful'), and the folded-map accordion built from canvas.toDataURL at unfold time (a multi-hundred-ms stall on a phone).
Letter-board character flips fire on every ranking or time change. With 15-minute scrub steps, that means constant flicker and DOM churn across 5 strips of 24 spans each.
Four families (Tilt Warp 68.7KB, League Gothic 18.7KB, Martian Mono 38.4KB, Atkinson 37.6KB) means four FOUT/fallback stacks to tune and four voices on a 390px screen.
Mobile: header 52 + folded map 152 + board header, hero line, sun rail and filters puts the first strip at about y=540. In a real ~650px Safari viewport, about one strip is visible.
The domino glyph is a comprehension gamble and the direction admits it may need replacing with text.
The receipt PNG relies on navigator.share({files}), which won't work inside the artifact.

strengths: The most performance-literate map spec: sprite traffic instead of a radial gradient per car per frame (my bench: the gradient path costs about 3x the sprite path), bloom on a 1/8-size offscreen canvas, an explicit 6ms frame budget, and auto-degrade after 3 frames over 20ms.
The Beacon card is the right product fix: one complete answer, the best move for this hour, rendered in the DOM on first paint and never blocked by the intro.
The strictest accent discipline. Beacon appears on one interactive element per view; everything else that glows is 'light', not brand.
The Sun Strip painted from the real light model, the 'SCRUBBING 1:30PM · REAL 4:42PM' line, role=slider and aria-valuetext fix r0's two-clock contradiction honestly.
A distance-from-coast water field (rasterize land to 512px, box-blur 3 times, read it as depth) is a one-time, cheap trick that would make the day map look like bathymetry instead of mint.
An honest truth line on the map ('traffic and boats illustrative') and the 'glow only what is actually open' rule tie the effects to real data.
Two families, and the only direction that names WCAG 2.3.1 flash limits.
weaknesses: It is the archetype the founder already rejected: a full-bleed dark map plus an opaque left board or bottom sheet. Polishing it harder still produces 'dark map template + sidebar', minus the glass.

All of the wow lives in one canvas renderer with 6-8 subsystems (water field, sprites, bloom, reflections, boats with Kelvin wakes, lights-on wave, glint, tilt). That is the hardest thing to make look finished in a day and the most likely to drop frames on a mid-range Android.

Caching 24 phase buckets means 24 full-screen bitmaps, about 5MB each at DPR 2 on a 390x844 phone, roughly 126MB. That invites an iOS tab kill. Two cached states with a cross-fade, as r0 already does, is the right size.
A CSS rotateX tilt of a flat canvas reads as a postcard tipping over, not a camera, and the spec disables taps while it runs.

The boats are invented decoration on a product whose brief says 'real or clearly labeled'. The pools are dead on arrival: geo.json has 0 pool features, and the direction's own rule says skip them if OSM doesn't supply them.
Science Gothic as the body face at 16px is a Bank Gothic revival doing paragraph work, and the file is 156KB.

Neon-over-dark Miami with a Bank Gothic lineage reads as Vice City fan art. The direction says GTA VI launches Nov 19, 2026, the day before the test trip. I could not verify that date this session; if it's true, the risk is acute.
The title-card axis morph (wdth 200 to the target, 40ms stagger per row) on every re-rank is visual noise while scrubbing.
Mobile budget: 388 + 40 + 230 + 56 + 64 = 778px before the safe area. It does not fit a real Safari or artifact viewport either.

judges.winner: Tear Here. It is the only direction whose concept lands with one object finished to polish plus a CSS color field, and the color field is both the cheapest and the biggest visual change.
